Yakub Ali, out of his 7.23½ acres land, sold 2.20 acres land to Ibrahim Khalil Majumder and others. Our of the remaining 4.53½ acres land, the heirs of Yakub Ali, Abdul Bari Miah, Abdul Ali Miah and Karamat Ali Miah, sold 4.53 acres land by two registered sale deeds dated 17.04.1926 in favour of Karimuddin Bepari, father of the pre-emptee and others and Karimuddin Bepari got only 0.5766 acre land. Karimuddin Bepari died leaving behind four sons including the pre-emptee two daughters and the pre-emptee got only 0.113 acre land in his share from his father, Karimuddin Bapari. The pre-emptee also purchased .0188 acre land from his two brothers and one sister. The pre-emptors transferred .10 acre land to one Abdul Ghani Master by registered sale deed dated 13.12.1953 and also sold .07 acre land to one Nurul Islam by registered deed of transfer dated 06.02.1987 and the pre-emptee sold more that his share in C.S. Khatian No. 17. The pre-emptee was a stranger to the case holding, so the pre-emptors were entitled to pre-empt the case land. 

 4. Subsequently, the preemption application was amended incorporating the fact the heirs of Yukyb Ali Munshi had shown transfer in respect of an area of 3 kanis, 2, gonads, 2 karas and 2 krantees equivalent to 3.76 acres land out of the disputed C.S. Khatian Nos. 17, 18, 19, 20 and 21 along with Khas Khatian No.1 and the schedule to the sale deed had shown that 2.63 acres land was sold from C.S. Kharian No.17. The pre-emptee had no interest in the case holding, whereas the per-emptors were co-sharers by inheritance as will as by purchase and as such, they were entitled to preempt the case lands. 

 5. The miscellaneous cases were contested by pre-emptee by filing separate written objection contending, inter alia, that he was a co-sharer in the case holding by inheritance, so preemption applications against him were not maintainable. Karimuddin Bepari, predecessor-in-interest of the pre-emptee and his three brothers purchased 3.76 acres land from the heirs of C.S. recorded tenant, Yukub Ali by registered deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 and Karimuddin got 0.94 acre land in the case holding in his share and he died leaving behind four sons named Abdul Ghani Master, the pre-emptee, Abdul Kader and Nurul Haque, two daughters-Zinnatunnessa and Arabunnessa and a widow, Faridunnessa died leaving behind four sons and two daughters named above. The pre-emptee inherited .18¾ acres land from his father, Karimuddin Bepari. The pre-emptee purchased .02¾ acre land from his sister-Zinnatunnessa. In the above manner, the pre-emptee became the owner and the possessor in respect of .21 2/15 acre land. The pre-emptee sold .17 acre land by two sale deeds and he remained the owner and possessor in respect of .21 2/15 acre land as co-sharer in the case holding. The pre-emptors and others got their holding separated on mutation in Mutation Case Nos.303 of 1987-88 and 296 of 1987-88 and opened new khatians being Khatian No.195 in respect of 4.30 acres land and Khatian No.188 in respect of 4.13 acres land and paid rents separately. Because of the separation of jamas, the per-emptors on longer remained a co-sharer in the case holding in S.A. Khatian No.10 covered by sale deed dated 20.01.1990 and 21.01.1990 (the deeds under preemption). Shamsuddin and his brothers-Fazlur Rahman and Khorshed Alom also got their 2.18 acres land separated from S.A Khatian No.10 in Mutation Case. No.301 of 1987-88 and paid rents separately. After purchase of the respective case land by separate deed under preemption, the pre-emptee made much improvement thereon, i.e. excavated pond, raised the land and constructed house and thereby incurred an expenditure of take 1,22,500.00. 

 "Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the petitions submits that though land of cadastral Survey Khatian Nos.18-21 had been shown as tenanted land in the sale deed dated 17.04.1926 under Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 but the said under tenancies subsequently got no existence as under tenancies and the said land went to khan holding of Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 and those land of under tenancies stood recorded in State Acquisition Khatian No.10 in the names of tenants or heirs of transferors Cadastral Survey Khatian No.17 and not in the names of heirs of any under tenants of Cadastral Survey Khatian Nos.18-21 and the deed of conveyance dated 17.04.1926 is a positive proof that Karim Uddin and his three (3) brothers purchased 3.76 acres of land from sons of Yakub Ali and Karim Uddin got. 94 acres of land in the case holding and pre-emptor-petitioner inherited .18-2 acres of land from his holding and father Karimuddin and pre-emptor petitioner still remains owner and co-sharer by way of inheritance in respect of li acres of land after transfer of .17 acres of land and pre-emptor petitioner having been a co sharer by way of inheritance, pre-emption cases by pre-emptor respondent is not at all maintain-able and both the trial Court and the Lower Appellate Court concurrently found that the pre-emptor petitioner is a co-sharer by inheritance and those findings rested upon correct construction and reading of the sale deed dated 17.04.1926, share of Yukub Ali in the case holding and materials on record but the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division totally misdirected himself in his approach in resolving the legal battle involved in pre-emption cases and committed a substantial error in holding that pre-emptor-petitioner inherited .13 acres of land and transferred .17 acres of land and thereby exhausted all his interest in case holding and became a stranger and this Division did not at all explore the legal controversy and in a summary way dismissed the leave petitions and judgment under challenge in Civil Review Petition may kindly be reviewed in the interest of justice. 

 Mr. Huq submits that the pre-emptor-respondent-side in Mutation and sub Division of Joint Tenancy and holding case Nos.303 of 1987-1988 and 296 of 1987-1988 got Joint Tenancy and Holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No.10 separated and sub division and got their names mutated in separate Khatians in respect of 4.13 acres respectively and predecessor vendors of per-emptee-petitioner Shasuddin and others in Mutation and Sub Division of Holding Case No.301 of 1987-1988 got their Holding Sub-division and separated on opening of new Khatian in respect of 2.18 acres of land and the original Joint Tenancy and holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No.10 gat no existence and pre-emptor respondent side and predecessor vendors of pre-emptor-petitioner who stepped in to shoes of predecessor vendor-respondents, no longer remained co-sharer of the transferred holding and the pre-emptor respondent side ceased to be co-sharer of the tenancy and holding i.e. State Acquisition Khatian No.10, and thus, had legal character and locus standi to exercise right of Pre-emption against Pre-emptee petitioner and though the learned Trial Court Judge and the Appellate Court Judge took into stock this fundamental aspect of the matter neither the High Court Division nor the Appellate Division took into consideration the same and ruminated the vital and core legal aspect of the matter and that in the event of consideration and meditation of this important aspect of the matter, the fate of Civil Revisions and Civil Petitions For Leave to Appeal would have been otherwise and Per-petitioner would have been graced with favorable verdict and, as such impugned judgment may kindly be reviewed to secure ends of justice." 

 9. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel for the appellants, has made his submissions in line with the leave granting order and in support of his submissions, he has referred time and again to the kabala dated 19.02.1962, i.e. exhibit-'6'. He has also referred to the mutation khatians by which the per-emptors got their land of the case khatian separated to emboldened his submission that by separating the jamas of the pre-emptors from the case khatian, they ceased to be co-sharers therein and therefore, they were not entitled to preempt the case land as co-sharers, but the High Court Division failed to consider this vital factual and legal aspect of the case in allowing the miscellaneous cases and this Court also failed to notice the said legal and factual aspect of the case and thus fell into an error in dismissing the leave petitions and the appeals merit consideration and the same be allowed. 

 10. Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Advocate fir respondent Nos.1(a) and 1(b) in both the appeals, has supported the judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as the judgment of this Division dismissing the leave petitions. He has submitted that against the finding of the trial Court that the per-emptors were co-sharers in the case holding, the pre-emptee filed a cross-objection before the District Judge and that was rejected. Therefore, the same question cannot be re-opened before this Court in these appeals, because the finding of the Appellate Court as to the co-sharership of the pre-emptor shall be a resjudicata in view of the provisions of section 11 of Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his contention, he has referred the case of G.H. Hook-Vs-Administrator General of Bengal and others, AIR 1921, Privy Council, H. Mr. Khair has further submitted that it is true that the pre-emptors got their jamas separated from the case khatian, but on their application, the lands of the khatians were again amalgamated during the pendency of the miscellaneous case, thereby, before the date of hearing of the cases, the co-sharership of the pre-emptors in the khatian was restored. Therefore, the High Court Division rightly allowed the miscellaneous cases and there being no merit in the appeals, the same be dismissed. 

 11. From the leave granting order quoted hereinbefore, it is clear that leave was granted to decide two points; one: whether the pre-emptee remained as a co-sharer in the case holding after transfer of the land by him as claimed by the pre-emptoes and two: whether the per-emptors ceased to be co-sharers in case holding after separation of the khatian in their names and whether the subsequent amalgamation of the khatian the pendency of the miscellaneous cases could have any legal consequence in restoring the co-sharership of the pre-emptors in the case khatian and thus give them locus standi to file the application for preemption as co-sharers. 

 12. We would like to deal with the second point first, because if it is found that the pre-emptors ceased to co-sharers in the case holding due to splitting of the jamas long before filing the miscellaneous cases and that the subsequent amalgamation of the khatians could not have any legal consequence on the pre-emptors claim of cosharership in the case khatian, that the other point need not be answered. 

 13. Admittedly, the jama of the pre-emptors was separated from the case khatian being S.A. Khatian No.10 and this is very much apparent from exhibit-'5', i.e. the order sheets of Miscellaneous Case No.2 of 1991-1992 in which the jamas were allegedly amalgamated. The two orders passed in the miscellaneous case read as follows: 

 14. Besides the orders passed in the above miscellaneous case, the fact of separation of khatian is further clear from the mutation being Nos.188, 195, 193 of the office of Assistant Commissioner (Land), Shahrasti, Chandpur. 

 15. Mr. Mahbubey Alam has pointed out that after the miscellaneous cases for pre-emption were filed on 16.05.1991, the pre-emptors with the other co-sharers filed an application under section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Shahrasti, Chandpur for reconsideration of the cases by which their janas were separated with the further prayer for cancellation of the mutation cases and also for amalgamation of S.A. Khatian No.10 and accordingly, a proceeding under the said section of the Act, 1950 was started. From the first order as quoted hereinbefore, it is clear that the jamas of the pre-emptors from the case khatian were separated and were approved, but they prayed for amalgamation on the plea that the jamas were separated on mistaken calculation of share of the co-sharers. The second order dated 30.03.1992 shows that the jamas were amalgamated by cancelling the earlier approved khatians after one year, two months of filing the miscellaneous cases and without assigning any cogent reason too for such amalgamation far from any finding that the jamas separated earlier was done on wrong calculation of share of the co-sharers. The only funny reason assigned by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) was that amalgamation was made to facilitate realization of government revenue and for maintaining the records properly ignoring the fact that after separation of the khatians, the pre-meptors paid rents for three years and during this period neither the Government nor the applicants before him faced any difficulty in paying rents as well as in realizing the same by the Government from the applicants. 

 16. It further appears that the jamas in question were separated on 20.01.1988 and 21.01.1988 respectively, whereas the prayer for preemption vide the miscellaneous cases were filed on 16.02.1991, i.e. the date on which the miscellaneous cases were filed, the pre-emptors were not co-sharers in the case khatian. Therefore, they were not entitled to preempt the case lands as co-sharers in the case khatian. It also appears to be very significant that the written objection in the respective miscellaneous case by the pre-emptee was filed on 05.08.1991 stating categorically that the pre-emptors ceased to be co-sharers in the case khatian as because they separated their khatians from the case khatian, whereas the application under section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 was filed on 18.03.1992. Thus, it is clear that the pre-emptors made a very smart move to review the order of separation of the khatians passed earlier in the above mentioned mutation cases just to obviate the legal stigma that since they ceased to be co-sharers in the khatian would have no locus standi to pray for preemption of the case lands transferred by the kabalas in question. 

 17. In the context, we find substance in the submission of Mr. Mahbubey Alam that if this kind of smart move by a pre-emptor(s) is allowed, the very act of separation of the khatians shall become an absolute mockery and in the process, the factual stand taken by the per-emptee in a preemption proceeding through the written objection as to the locus standi of the pre-emptor(s) shall be rendered ineffective and nugatory by the post facto move of the pre-emptor(s) and a Court of law cannot be a party to such a move of the pre-emptor(s). 

 18. Besides the above, the order of amalgamation passed by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) prima facie was not done in accordance with law inasmuch as from the order dated 18.03.1992, it is clear that the application was filed by the pre-emptors along with others under section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 for reviewing the earlier order of separation of the khatians, but the order was passed for amalgamation of the khatians. This move was possibly taken by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) as proviso (c) to section 150(1) has clearly provided that an order shall not be modified or reversed on a review until reasonable notice has been given to the parties concerned to appear and be heard in the matter, but the orders as quoted hereinbefore do not show that any notice was at all given to the parties concerned and a date was fixed for such hearing after service of notice. 

 19. In the context, we would like to point out that section 150 of Act, 1950 is in Chapter XVIII under the head Jurisdiction, Appeal, Revision and Review, whereas amalgamation, subdivision and consolidation of holdings is in Chapter XV and for the amalgamation of a holding, completely separated procedure has been laid down in this chapter, whereas the procedure of review as provided in section 150 is quite different. More significant thing is that clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 150 has clearly provided that an application for review of an order shall not be entertained unless it is made within thirty days from the date of such order or, when such application is presented after the expiry of the said period of thirty days, unless the applicant satisfies the Revenue Officer that he had sufficient cause for not making the application within the said period. But unfortunately the orders of the Assistant Commissioner (Land) do not show any reflection whatsoever of the said provisions of clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 150. In the instant case, the application for review was filed long after 3(three) years of the separation of the jamas, but the orders show that no application was filed for condoning the delay after such an inordinate delay. Therefore, the order of amalgamation made by the Assistant Commissioner (Land) having not been done in accordance with law, the same was illegal and an inconsequential order and the same could not in any way save the pre-emptors to be strangers in the case holding in view of the separation of the khatian made earlier. 

 20. It is also an admitted fact that after separation of the khatians for long three years, the pre-emptors enjoyed its benefit and paid rents, but they shifted from their said stand only to avail their right of pre-emption as co-sharers in the case holding by filing application under section 150(1) for reviewing the case of separation of the jamas. Such a move was absolutely malafide just to negate the provisions of law and cannot be approved by a Court of law. We conclude that the very date on which the cause of action to file the pre-emption applications arose the pre-emptors not being co-sharers in the case khatian, were not entitled to pray for preemption of the case lands as co-sharers in the case kharian. 

 22. This finding of the trial Court clearly shows that it did not at all consider the fact that the pre-emptors though filed the application under section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 for reviewing the cases of earlier separation of khatian, but the order was passed for amalgamation just in a casual manner on the reasons reasons already discussed above. The trial Court also failed to consider that the application for reviewing the separation of the khatian was filed after one year, four months of filing the application for preemption and also after filing the written objection by the pre-emptee where he specifically pleaded that pre-emptors ceased to be co-sharers in the case holding due to the separation of the jamas from the case khatian. It is true that a cross-objection was filed by the pre-emptee against this finding before the District Judge when pre-emptors filed the miscellaneous appeals against the order of the trial Court rejecting the prayer for preemption and the same was rejected, but as it appears that the Appellate Court like the trial Court did not at all consider the provisions of section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 as discussed above and the glaring attending fact that the application under the said section was filed long after filing the miscellaneous cases and filing the written objection taking objection that the pre-emptors ceased to be co-sharers in the kharian as they separated their jamas from the case khatian and without giving any explanation for filing the same after such a long delay. This will be clear from the finding of the first Appellate Court. The finding so far as it relates to the rejection of cross-objection by the first Appellate Court is as under: 

 23. The finding of the Appellate Court clearly shows that it did not also at all consider the facts and circumstances of the case under which the order of amalgamation of the khatians was passed. Since the Appellate Court failed to consider provisions of section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 in rejecting the cross-objection filed by the pre-emptee against the finding of the trial Court as the co-sharership of the pre-emptors its finding in that respect was perincuriam. Further the Appellate Court totally misconceived the doctrine of lis pendens and also totally failed to consider that the act of amalgamation of the khatains of the  pre-emptors on the basis of an application under section 150(1) of the Act, 1950 during the pendency of the miscellaneous cases was not a case of lis pendens within the meaning of section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, but a malafide and smart move made by the pre-emptors to acquire the locus standi to file the application for preemption by resorting to amalgamating the khatains which stood separated long three years before and had already been acted upon. Therefore, we find no sub-stance in the submission of Mr. Khair Ezaz Maswood that the question of re-opening the separation of khatians touching the cessation of co-sharership of the pre-emptors would be a resjudicata within the meaning of section 11 of the Code. The facts and circumstances of the case under which the Privy Council propounded the principle of resjudicata in the case of G.H. Hook (supra) are absolutely distinguishable from the instant case and hence the principle of law enunciated therein has no manner of application in the instant case.

full_judgment:
4. That RS Khatian No. 2629/21 appertaining to RS plot No. 13119 and 13109 comprising an area of 0.10 + 0.06 = 0.16 acre were recorded in the names of Ahammad Khalil and Ahammad Kabir to the extent of 4 annas and 16 gandas each and the remaining 6 annas 8 gandas were recorded in the name of Hafizur Rahman, who by amicable settlement with other co-sharers lived in 0.6 acre homestead portion and same was recorded in his name. In this way plaintiff Nos. 1-16 inherited through their predecessor Aminulla 0.07 1/4 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/15, .04 from RS Khatian No. 2926/16, 0.34 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/17, 0.17 acre from RS Khatian No. 2926/18 and 0.6 acre from RS Khatian No, 2926/21 totaling an area of 0.68 1/4 acre of land. The plaintiff Nos.1-16 have got their right, title interest and possession in the schedule properties. The defendant Nos. 3-16 are co-sharers of the disputed khatians for which they have been impleaded as defendants to avoid defect of parties. Since the names of other defendants are wrongly recorded in the BS khatian, they have also been impleaded in the suit. It was further stated in the plaint that the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, Md Abdul Monayem filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for Khas possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 against three sons of Aminulla, Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah. They appeared in the said suit and filed joint written statement stating that they have no knowledge about Other Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit no notice was served upon the defendant and the decree was collusive, no auction sale was held in Decree Execution Case on 27-1-1954 and there was no commission report by the Advocate Commissioner and delivery of possession of the Property on 11-4-1957 through court. Ultimately the above suit was dismissed on compromise. In fact Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal, void, inoperative and without jurisdiction. The plaintiff tried to compromise the matter with the defendants through the arbitration of local Commissioner, but the defendants did not appear. Subsequently, the defendants with a view to harass the plaintiffs filed Non-GR No. 468 of 1986 under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Criminal Case No. 254 of 1990, and Panchlaish GR Case No. 33(8) of 1990 in local Police Station against the plaintiffs. The cause of action arose on 19-9-1991 when the defendants threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess them. Subsequently, by amending the plaint the plaintiff prayed for a declaration that the decree dated 31-7-1952 passed by the Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and auction sale held on 27-9-1954 in Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 are null and void, ineffective, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs and for partition. 

 5. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the said suit by filing joint written statement denying all the materials allegation made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in the present form, there is no cause of action and the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the same is not maintainable without prayer for declaration of title and khas possession and further the suit is barred by waiver, Estoppel and acquiescence, the principle of res-judicata, defect of parties and also barred by limitation. The positive case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are that the predecessor of the defendants are that, Abdul Monayem obtained the preliminary decree in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 on 31-7-1952 passed by the Munsif Fifth Court, Chittagong against Moulvi Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs in respect of the land described in the suit schedule alongwith other property. Accordingly, final decree was prepared on 5-3-1953 in which the decree-holder got saham of 0.342/7 acre in his share from RS plot No. 13104 and 13108. Thereafter in respect of cost of the suit he filed Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 in which he purchased 0.06 acre of land in auction sale from RS plot No. 13109 and took delivery of possession through court on 11-4-1957. Aminulla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was permitted to live in RS plot No. 13108 temporarily, but after his death his three sons Tazul Huda, Serajul Huq and Hedayetullah refused to surrendered possession to the predecessor of the defendants and for which he filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 in the Court of Fifth Munsif, Chittagong for eviction. Ultimately the suit was dismissed in terms of solenama on 16-8-1969. 

 7. The plaintiffs have field the instant suit without paying required court fee on proper valuation of the suit land. These defendant along with other co-sharers are in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years by paying rents regularly, receiving rent-receipts. Hence they have got the absolute right, title, interest and possession over the suit land which the Plaintiffs have got no right to deny. The defendants have filed criminal case No. 523 of 1990 against the plaintiffs for theft of their fish from the pond of RS plot 13105 perhaps in turn of which they might have filed the present test suit which deserves to be dismissed. In fact the plaintiffs are well aware of the Final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and the auction sale which have been purchased by the predecessor of the defendants and all other deeds also. It is utter surprise to mentioned that where the plaintiffs have already admitted in their plaint about the sole decree dated 16-8-1969 passed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 how they can file the instant suit. Their predecessor-in-interest have specifically admitted the conditions save and except the possession of 0.07 acre of homestead land of RS plot No. 13108 they would never claim their previously sold out properties of all other khatians to the predecessor of the defendants. As per sole decree the predecessor of the defendants, Abdul Monayem had recorded his name correctly in BS khatian Nos. 693 and 695 which have finally been published in his name. After death, his heirs and subsequent heirs transferred 0.39 acre of land from BS plot Nos. 13252 and 13253 to Ashekane Awlia Abdul Monayem High School by registered Deed of Gift No. 7542 dated 1.6-12-1987 and delivered possession, which is within the schedule described in the plaint. Having been well aware of all these facts and circumstances, the plaintiffs intentionally did not make these defendants as parties to the suit. Now the defendants along with their transfers are, in fact, is in possession of their respective lands about which the plaintiffs are not at all entitled to claim any decree and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Defendant no. 24 contested the suit by filing a separate written statement wherein he also stated all the facts of final decree of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Decree Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 and reiterated the same facts as stated in the written statement filed on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1-2. It was further stated that Abdul Monayem executed registered Wasiatnama No. 34 dated 31-12-1974 in favour of sons and daughters relinquishing all his properties including the land of the schedule khatians of the suit. After his death, his daughter Mst Numahar Begum having been in possession of her properties died leaving 2 sons 5 daughters and husband as her legal heirs. Her husband Md Ismail Hossain Seraji executed another registered Wasiatnama No. 25 dated 19-7-1995 in favour of his two sons Md Aminul Islam and Azizul Islam. Thereafter Aminul Islam and Azizul Islam having acquired the property by way of Wasiatnama from father, by way of inheritance from their mother and 2 daughter of Abdul Monayem Tahera Parvin and Farida Yasmin having from mother by way of inheritance jointly transferred by kabala No. 4340 dated 5-8-1996 to this defendant from RS plot No. 13104 an area of 8 gandas 2 karas 2 kranti and 1 1/2 danta Ithiti land and handed over possession to this defendant. This defendant having delivery of possession of his purchased land constructed boundary walls around the land and pucca gate where he engraved his name and has been possessing peacefully since purchase. He was not aware of the suit and he was not made party to the suit. Having been informed from reliable source he appeared with a prayer to be added as party in the suit and was made party on his prayer. All the claims of the plaintiffs are false. They cannot deny the decree and decree execution case. This defendant is in possession of his purchased property by paying rent, cesses and receiving rent receipts. The suit is hopelessly barred by the principles of waiver, estoppel Acquiescence and also barred by limitation and res-judicata and is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. The learned Joint District Judge upon consideration of materials evidence on record by his judgment dated 25-11-2008 decreed the suit. Against the said decree, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 in the Court District Judge, Chittagong and in due course appeal was transferred to the Additional District Judge, First Court, Chittagong. In Title Appeal No. 16 of 2009 plaintiff filed an application on 13-6-2010 calling for the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 of Fifth Munsif Court, Chittagong and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 of the same court describing the papers and documents in the said application and same was rejected by the appellate court by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010. Ultimately, the learned Additional District Judge after hearing the parties, dismissed the appeal by judgment and decree dated 9-9-2010 and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 12. During pendency of the revisional application before this court, the petitioner filed an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 10-3-2013 for additional evidence stating the facts that the record of the Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 were called for in the present Other Class Suit No. 137 of 2001 and the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was transmitted to the trial court but record of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 could not be transmitted as it was found missing at the relevant time. But due to bonafide Mistake of the learned Advocate for the defendants as well as the trial court the relevant order of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 was not exhibited. On the basis of such bonafide mistake, both the courts below erroneously found that the defendants did not take steps to prove the service of summons of Other Class Suit No. 39 of 1950 which was duly served upon the defendants. But on scrutinizing the order sheet of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, it appears that the defendant No. 1 Aminulla, the predecessor of the present plaintiffs was appeared in that suit and filed written statement on 22-2-1951 (order No.8) It also transpired from the order sheet of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 that the defendant (present plaintiff) appeared in that title suit and filed written statement and ultimately the suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn upon. It is pertinent to mentioned here that those documents were submitted by the plaintiffs in the appellate court but the appellate court below did not consider those documents as additional evidence. It was further stated that the record of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 are now before this hon'ble court and the petitioners on the advice of their learned Advocate collected certified copy of entire order sheet of Title Suit 53 of 1968 and written statement filed by defendants dated 10-3-1969. From those documents it will be crystal clear that summons were duly served upon the defendants in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 and they have contested the said suit by filing written statements in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 respectively. It is also stated that in paragraph No. 2 of the plaint of the present suit the plaintiffs admitted that they appeared and filed written statements in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968. Since the plaintiffs are admitting the facts of their appearance in the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, which can be easily taken as additional evidence, as admitted facts need not be proved. 

 14. It is also denied that the decree holder Abdul Munayem gave 0.7 acre land to Aminullah for residing there temporary as licensee. It was further denied that Tajul Huda and his two brothers appeared and filed written statement on 10-3-1969 or on any other date in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 filed by Abdul Munayem. It is also denied that they filed a compromise petition on 7-8-1969 or any on other date and on the basis of said compromise petition suit was decreed. It was further stated that defendants had ample opportunities to exhibit the order sheet of Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 and both the courts below have given their findings on the decree passed in Other Suit No. 39 of 1950, the Execution Case arising there from and on Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and hence the petitioners are not entitled to adduce additional evidence before the revisional court to patch up the weak part of their case which is not permissible under Order XII, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 15. Mr Khalilur Rahman with Mr Khalilur Rahman(Helal) and Mr Mohammad Zafar Ali Khan, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the Defendant-petitioners. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners firstly, submits that the present suit was filed on 28-9-1991 challenging the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, and the plaintiffs had knowledge about filing of earlier Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which they have admitted in paragraph no. 2 of the plaint of the present suit. Since the present suit is filed long after 23 years from their knowledge, same is hopelessly barred by limitation. Secondly, Mr Khalil, submits that in respect of suit property, Abdul Munayem, father of the defendant nos. 1-2 filed Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 against the predecessors of the plaintiffs Aminullah who contested the said partition suit by filing written statement and ultimately preliminary and final decree was passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. Thereafter, the predecessors of the defendant again filed Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessor of the plaintiffs, Aminullah who appeared and contested the Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement on 10-3-1969 and the said suit was decreed on compromise on 7-8-1969. Thirdly, learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs claimed title in the suit on the basis of korfa lease of their predecessors Aminullah and RS khatian was published in the name of their predecessor but they, failed to file any lease deed as such korfa lease and record of right does not create any title in the suit land. So, after passing of the final decree in a Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and compromise decree dated 7-8-1969 between the parties, and for the same self suit land, the present second suit is barred under the principles of res-judicata and not maintainable. Since the trail court failed to frame any issue in the present suit, whether the suit is barred by res-judicata and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Fourthly, the learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs has miserably failed to prove that fraud was committed in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 and also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Fifthly, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents. Sixthly, he submits that the plaintiff failed to established their title in the suit land, so they cannot challenge the title deeds of the defendants, who acquired title through the process of law. He lastly submits that both the courts below totally failed to consider the evidence, both oral and documentary and misread and non-considered the materials evidence on record and thus committed gross error of law in not dismissing the suit. Accordingly, the learned Advocate prayed that the rule should be made absolute. 

 17. On the other hand, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali, the learned Advocate submits that the suit is not barred by limitation because of the fact that the previous suit being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 filed by Abdul Munayam, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 of the present suit and the defendants Aminullah, predecessors of the present plaintiffs are not aware about the final decree passed in that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that no summons were served upon the defendants in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the said decree was obtained by practicing fraud, then auction sale held in other Execution Case No. 18 of 1953 were not effective and thus the suit is not barred by limitation and same are not binding upon the plaintiffs. In support of his submission he referred two decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 and 19 DLR (SC) 433, He further submits that the lower appellate court concurred with the findings of the trial court that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land, thus the plaintiffs suit for declaration of title and partition is not barred by limitation. 

 He next submits that the defendants have failed to prove that the predecessor of the plaintiffs signed the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 which was affirmed by the appellate court. Therefore, the present suit is not barred by the principles of res-judicata and waiver. He also submits that the trial court found that the RS record prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs during the period from 1924 to 1930 in Chittagong region same has presumptive value and the defendants did not challenge the same in any court of law. The predecessors of the plaintiffs-Aminuddin being korfa lessee and his successors continued in possession for more than 12 years and on the basis of the RS khatian they acquired title in the suit land. In this respect he placed reliance two decisions reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287 and 54 DLR (AD) 173. He then submits that both the courts below concurrently found that the decree in the Other Suit No. 39 of 1950 was void and defendants did not try to prove by sufficient evidence that the solenama filed in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 was actually executed by the three sons of Aminullah and therefore the defendants did not acquire any title by the said deeds, further the defendants did not appear in Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 by filing written statement and compromise petition have been filed fraudulently by the plaintiffs of that suit. Since both the courts below concurrently found that the judgment and decree in the earlier partition suit are void, in-operative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Therefore, the present partition suit filed by the plaintiffs is quite maintainable and it is not necessary to have a separate decree for cancellation of the registered two deeds of the defendants. He further submits that both the courts below in consideration of the evidence, found that the deeds through which the defendants claimed title did not confer any title or possession on the defendants and gave cogent reasons in support of their findings and the courts had jurisdiction to consider whether the deeds conferred title or possession on the defendants even though some of those were 30 years old documents and the genuineness of such documents may be challenged and there is no misreading or nonconsideration of the material evidence by the courts below and the defendants are not entitled to challenge those findings. In this connection he refers the decision reported in 17 BLD (AD) 199. He also submits that the trial court found that the defendants claimed that Abdus Sabur is the owner of land described in the first schedule to the plaint, and in that case the onus is upon the defendant to prove the claim of ownership of Abdus Sabur but they did not file any documents in support of the ownership of Abdus Sabur. DW 1 in his cross-examination admitted that he did not know about any deed showing title of Abdus Sabur. Moreover the document dated 19-6-1895 shows that in that deed ten gandas of land stating Moghi dags were mentioned. But in the written statement the corresponding CS and RS dags had not been mentioned. The defendants did not adduce any documentary or oral evidence to show that the land mentioned in the above deed dated 19-6-1895 and the lands described in the schedule to the plaint are the same land. He also submits that the RS khatian have got presumptive value relating to title in the Chittagong region and the RS record was prepared in Chittagong region from the years 1924 to 1930. After settlement with Aminulla, Abul Bashar and Ithairul Bashar have no title in the land settled with Aminulla. Since the korfa settlement was coupled with possession, the defendants are not entitled to challenge the settlement of Aminulla after 12 years from the time of preparation of RS khatian. He further submits that the defendants fails to prove that Aminulla the predecessor of the plaintiff are in permissive possession of some land was not prove either in the earlier suit or in the present suit. So, the auction was not effective and hence the defendants did not acquire any,title in the land allegedly sold in auction. He finally submits that the application regarding the additional evidence as provided under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure prescribed that the need for additional evidence must be felt by the court itself. This provision of law is clearly not intended to allow a litigant who has been unsuccessful in the lower court to fill up the omission. In this respect he referred to a decision reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220 and accordingly prayed for discharged of the Rule. 

 21. It further appears that earlier the suit land was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950, which was filed by the predecessor of the present defendants against the predecessor of the present plaintiffs, Aminulla and others and got a decree. In support of their claim defendants exhibited the preliminary decree (Exhibit-Ka), final decree with Advocate Commissioner report (Exhibit-kha), certified copy of the order sheet of original Execution Case No. 18 of 1953, Sale Certificate dated 8-4-1954 (Exhibit-Gha), certificate of delivery of possession dated 11-4-1957 (Exhibit-Ga) and kabala No. 3139 dated 5-6-1951 in favour of defendant No. 1.  But both the courts below failed to consider those documents of the defendants and erroneously found that by the said documents the defendants, present petitioners did not get any decree in the said suit. 

 22. It also appears that the predecessor of the present defendant filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the present plaintiffs and in that title suit defendant appeared and filed written statement and said suit was decreed on compromise and accordingly compromise decree was drawn. To prove such facts the present defendants filed the application for compromise (Exhibit-Ja) and the sole decree (Exhibit-Ja(1) respectively, wherefrom it is evident that three sons of Aminulla executed the said solenama, but both the courts below failed to consider such vital aspect of the case and erroneously found that the defendants could not prove the said facts. It further transpires that the defendants filed an applications before the appellate court on 13-6-2010 for calling for the records of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968, Title Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. The appellate court heard this application and rejected the same by order No. 17 dated 14-7-2010 on the ground that— “আপীলকারী বিবাদীপক্ষে আনীত দরখাস্তটি অনাবশ্যক বিধায় আপাতত না মঞ্জুর করা হইল, তবে অত্র মোকদ্দমার আপীল শুনানীঅন্তে উক্ত দরখাস্তের বিষয়বস্তু বিবেচনাযোগ্য। 

 26. The learned Advocate for the defendants petitioners strenuously argued that the High Court Division conferred wide power in order to do justice in a case and it shows that in the instant case the appellate court failed to exhibits the aforesaid vital documents although the same was also filed before the appellate court but those documents were not considered at the time of hearing of the appeal. After consideration and appreciation of the materials and evidence on record it appears that the documents and papers filed by the defendants-petitioners are very much necessary for proper adjudication of the suit. It is, however, felt that ends of justice will be meet if both the parties should be given opportunity to prove their case by filing those documents in appellate court. In this connection reference is made to the case of Sunil Krishna Banki vs Kailash Chandra Saha reported in 36 DLR (AD) 220. Since the court below totally misread and non-considered the Exhibits namely, Exhibit Nos. Ka to Umo, Exhibit Nos. Ja and J(1) and also did not call for the record of the Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 which is very much material to consider that whether the present defendants, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 obtain any decree fraudulently against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs. The opposite parties has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 137 of 2001 seeking, firstly prayed for declaration that both preliminary and the final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and also the decree passed in Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 are illegal collusive and fraudulent, Secondly, the BS khatian No. 693 and 695 are wrong and baseless and also for partition of total 0.90 acres land claiming entire 0.64 1/4 acres which was partitioned in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950. In that suit the predecessors of the defendant Nos. 1-2, Md Abdul Monayem was the plaintiff and predecessors of the present plaintiffs Aminullah was the defendant. 

 27. On going through the materials on record it is apparent that the heirs of the defendant of the earlier suit were all out to deprive the plaintiff of the said suit of the fruit of the decree and as last resort has filed the present Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 on 28-9-1991 after 41 years of the first suit and 23 years of the second suit seeking the relief primarily by way ul setting aside the decrees that were passed in those two suits under the shadow of the relief seeking separate saham in respect of the schedule land. It is seen from the materials on record and admitted by the plaintiffs of the present suit that the land which was the subject matter of Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 has also been made subject matter of present Other Suit No, 92 of 1991. 

 28. It is not disputed from the side of the plaintiffs that relief sought for in Other Suit No. 92 of 1991 relates to seeking set aside the decree passed in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Title Suit No. 53 of 1968 but the courts below failed to frame any issue whether the decisions made in the former suits operates as res-judicata in the present suit. 

 30. It appears that in respect of the suit land preliminary and final decree was passed on 11-8-1953 in Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and the defendants took possession of 34 2/7 acres of their saham on 20-6-1956 though court in Execution Case No. 18 of 1953. Thus after passing of the final decree in the said partition suit between the same parties, the second suit filed by the plaintiffs after 41 years is not maintainable and is barred by limitation. So, the decisions referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167 is not applicable in the present case. In the present suit, the plaintiffs have miserably failed to prove that the decree obtained fraudulently in the earlier suits being Partition Suit No. 39 of 1950 and Other Suit No. 53 of 1968 against the predecessors of the present plaintiffs and that the plaintiffs also failed to prove that the summons were not duly served upon them in earlier suits. Further, both the courts below failed to consider that most of the title deeds of the present defendants are 30 years old documents, but without considering this legal aspect of the suit, the courts below erroneously passed the decree declaring that those documents are forged documents.

2. The relevant facts for the disposal of the appeal, in short, are that the appellants instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title in the suit covering an area of 1.20 acres of C.S. Plot No. 1 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 53 of Mouza Kakrail., Police Station Ramna, (former Keranigonj) Dhaka alleging, inter alia, that the suit land along with other lands measuring 48.90 acres of said Plot and Khatian corresponding to S.A. Plot No.64 and S.A. Khatian No. 26 originally belonged to Bhawal Zaminder Rajkumer Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury who settled the suit land to Ashraf Ali Kazi, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs executing a pattannama on 05.02.1905. Said Ashraf Ali Kazi took over possession of the suit land and paid rent to the Zaminder. In C.S. operation, the suit land along with other lands of the disputed jam, was recorded in the name of Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Against the said record of right Ashraf Ali Kazi filed objection to get the same corrected and got an order on 24.05.1925. In S.A. operation the same was again recorded in the name of Public Works Department. On 12.01.1992, the plaintiffs discovered the pattannama, rent receipts and mutated C.S. Khatian in an old box in their house. On 08.03.1992, they collected the certified copies of the S.A. and C.S. Khatians and confirmed about the erroneous preparation of S.A. record of right. Thereafter, they filed this suit. 

 3. The defendant-respondents contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the that the suit land along with other lands covering 48.90 acres originally belonged to Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Accordingly, the same was recorded in C.S. Plot No. 1 and khatian No. 53. Subsequently the Deputy. Commissioner, Dhaka took over possession of the suit land. The story of settlement of the plaintiffs from Bhawal Rajkumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury is false and the document produced by the plaintiffs are forged and fabricated. The C.S. Khatian had not been corrected at the instance of the plaintiffs' predecessor. The corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs is forged. The Government has been possessing the suit land. The Government started to construct buildings in the suit land for residential purpose of higher Government Officials. The S.A. record of right was duly prepared in the name of the Government. The suit should be dismissed. 

 6. Mr. A.F. Hasan Arif, the senior Counsel 'appearing on behalf of the appellants, submits that the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff-appellants got the suit land by way of settlement in the year 1905 and produced more than 30 years old pattannama (exhibit-1) . The plaintiffs paid rents to the Zaminder vide Exhibit-2 series and they got the C.S. Khatian corrected vide exhibit-3 series and had been possessing the suit land more than 87 years. The third Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in disbelieving the pattannama, corrected C.S. Khatian and rent receipts. He submits that the findings of the third Judge of the High Court Division regarding authenticity of exhibit-1 made in an old British Indian Stamp of 1905, and the rent receipts (exhib-it-2 series), the corrected C.S. Khatian (exhibit 3 series) and exhibit-4, the volume book of Government containing C.S. Khatian are erroneous. He further submits that since price of the land was Tk. 15/- only as it appears in the pattannama, the same was not required to he registered under section 17 of the Registration Act. 

 7. Mr. Goutom Kumar, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the High Court Division on vivid discussions on the materials on record came to the conclusion that the pattannama, rent receipts of the Zamindar and corrected C.S. Khatian are forged and fabricated documents. He submits that Mr. Justice Md. Abdur Rashid rightly directed to prosecute the plaintiff-appellants initiating proceeding under Section 476 read with 195 (1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, on allegation of forging those documents. He submits that the plaintiffs had no title-and possession in the suit land. The Government, constructing the buildings in the suit land; has been possessing the same. The instant suit was not at all maintainable without the prayer for recovery of khas possession. 

 9. The case of the plaintiffs is that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi took settlement of the suit land on the basis of pattannama dated 05.02.1995 (exhibit-i). P.W.1 Abdul Matin Kazi, who was about 67 years old at the time of adducing his evidence on 19.08.1994 (that is, he was born after 22 years of alleged execution of the said pattannama) in his evidence, inter alia, said, এই সেই পত্তন নামার মূল কপি প্রঃ- ১ হিসাবে চিহ্নিত। কোর্ট দাখিল করিলাম। বিবাদীপক্ষে এই মর্মে আপত্তি যে, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। নোটারি পাবলিক কর্তৃক প্রত্তন নামার সত্যায়িত টাইপ কপি দাখিল করিলাম। প্রঃ ১(ক) আপত্তি সহকারে”। The is, exhibit-1 and 1(Ka) had been admitted in evidence with objection. The plaintiffs examined P.W.2 Sailendra Nath Sarker, a man of 78 years old, to prove the pattannama. In his cross-examination he said " ১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারব না।" From his evidence it appears that this witness was horn sometime in 1916, that is, after 11 years of the alleged execution of the pattannama. In order to substantiate the contents of the pattannama, the plaintiffs produced a notarized copy of the said pattannama exhibit-1(ka) P.W. 2 admitted that contents of the exhibit-1 are not readable. The plaintiffs did not examine the writer of the duplicated pattannama nor they examined the notary public, who notarized the same. In such view of the matter, Ext.1(Ka) could not be relied on. In the case of Harihar Prashad Vs. Desnarain reported in AIR 1956 SC 305 it was observed that the presumption enacted in Section 90 of the Evidence Act can be raised only with reference to original documents not to copies thereof. Furthermore, it appears that from Ext.1(Ka) that Ext.1 had been executed by Sree Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya on behalf of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. The P.W. 2, who claimed to be the Tahsilder of Bhawal Estate and joined in the said Estate in 1346 B.S., did not say in his evidence that Sree Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya was the Manager of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, the Zaminder of Bhawal Estate. The plaintiffs failed to produce any other evidence to prove that Kamini Kumar Bandapadhya was the manager of the Estate. 

 10. Submission of Mr. Arif is that since the Ext. 1 Pattannama is an old document of more than 30 years and had been produced from proper custody, the court would presume that the signature and every other part of Ext.1 is that person's hand writing and, the same had been duly executed by the person by whom it purports to be executed as per provision of Section 90 of the Evidence Act. The spirit of section 90 of the Evidence Act is that if private documents not less than thirty years old are produced from proper custody and are on their face free from suspicion, the court may presume at they w have been signed or written by the persons whose signatures they bear or in whose hand writing they purport to he, that they have been duly attested and executed, if they purport so to he Section 90 only lays down that the court may presume that document purporting to be 30 years old are genuine. That it must not presume them to be so. Supreme Court of India in the case of Sri Lakhi Baruah Vs. Sri Padma Kanta Kalita reported in AIR 1996 SC 1253 observed that Section 90 of the Evidence Act is founded on necessity and convenience because it is extremely difficult and sometimes not possible to lead evidence to prove handwriting, signature or execution of old documents after lapse of 30 years. In order to obviate such difficulties or improbabilities to prove execution of an old documents section 30 has been incorporated in the Evidence Act, which does away with the strict rule of proof of private documents. Presumption of genuineness may he raised if the document in question is produced from proper custody. It is, however, the discretion of the Court to accept the presumption flowing from Section. The presumption is permissive and accordance no the circumstances of each case the court may or may not raise it. That is, such presumption discretionary and so where a document is suspicious on the face of it or mutilated, the court may refuse to make presumption. It is not obligatory on a court to raise the presumption. The language being "may" when the person who has been examined as P.W.2 to prove the Ext.1 himself has said “১নং প্রদর্শনী পড়তে পারবো না"; then why the court will rely upon such document .At the time of making exhibit the defendant raised objection saving, লেখা অষ্পষ্ট ও ছেড়া প্রঃ ১টি। In such circumstances, the provision of section 90 ought to be applied with more care and great caution because nothing can he more easy than, for an unscrupulous ours person, who is wrongfully in possession and wants to make out a title to it to forge such document in his favour more than 30 years old and produce it as the proper custodian relieving himself of the necessity of proving its execution. The Ext. 1 patina must not be presumed to he genuine merely from its being ancient. Some other evidence were required to be given of the early existence and publicity of Ext. 1 . Neither C. S. khatian nor S. A. khatian had been prepared on the basis of Ext. 1. 

 11. In order to show the existence and publicity of Ext.1 or in other words to prove the story of their settlement dated 11.02.1905 and rebut the presumption under Section 103. B of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which is available in favour of the Government since C.S. record of right was prepared in favour of the Government ( Ext. A), the plaintiffs produced Ext .2 series, the Zamindari dakhilas and alleged corrected khatian Ext. 3 series. It is the claim of the plaintiffs that against C.S. Khatian their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi filed Objection Case No. 327H/1932 and got his name corrected in the Zamindery Sherista and obtained certified copies of the corrected Khatian from Zamindery sherist- Correction of the entry in Khatian filing objection in the Zamindery Sherista is totally illegal. As per provision of Section 108A of the Bengal Tenancy Act, which was transferred as section 115B, by the Bengal Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1928, only the Revenue Officer specially empowered by the Government on application or of his own motion, within two years (earlier time limit was for 12 months) from the date of certificate of the final publication of the record of right under sub-section (2) of Section 103A, correct any entry in such record of rights which he was satisfied had been made owing to a bonafide mistake. That is, Revenue Officer was legally authorized to correct the Khatian nobody else. The concerned volume regarding P.S. Khatian was called for to ascertain the authenticity of Ext. 3 series which was marked as Ext. 4 . T. Islam, J examined Ext. 3 series, the corrected Khatian produced by the plaintiffs and relevant volume book of C.S. khatian Ext. 4 thoroughly. Such examination, as it appears from his observation that the same was made most carefully which is praise-worthy. 

 "I have gone through Ext. 4, which is the volume of Mouza 282 Kakrail produced before the trial court. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13, 24, 53 and 55 as contained in Ext. 4, on the top of the front page at the left hand side under the heading  উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words "ভারত সম্রাট" have been printed and out of the above Khatian at the right hand side of the Khatian Nos. 1, 2, 9-10, 13-24 under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে বিস্তারিত দখল the names of different persons were printed and in the remaining C.S. Khatian Nos. 53 and 57, under this very heading at right hands side, public works Department and District Board respectively, both on behalf of Bharat Samrat were printed. In C.S. Khatian Nos. 3, 4, 5, 6 and 17 as contained in Ext. 4 similarly under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the word পত্তন রাজেন্দ্র নারায়ণ রায় ৩নং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and out of the above khatian under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল of C.S. Khatian Nos.  4,5 and 6 the names of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3 and 7 only, and this heading " কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস’"Were printed. 

 In C.S. Khatian Nos. 31-32, 33Ka, 34-35, 39-40, 43, 46-47 and 47Ka as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্তস্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words পত্তনী কালীন নারায়ন রায় ৩০নং দখল কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্���ারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed and in C.S. Khatian No. 8, as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিস্থ স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words মিরস জামাল, ৭নং রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ড were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Sheikh Abdul was printed. 

 In C.S. Khatian Nos. 30, 51Ka and 51 Kha as contained in Ext. 4, under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words সিকিম তালুক রামকৃষ্ণ দত্ত were printed and out of the above Khatians, in C.S. Khatian No. 30 under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the words কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী ওয়ারিশগণ পক্ষে কোর্ট অফ ওয়ার্ডস were printed and in Khatian No. 51 Ka and 51 Kha under the above heading of অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the names of other persons were printed. 

 In C.S. Khatian No. 25-27 and 51 as contained in Ext. 4 under the heading উপরিসত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words and also the names of 13 co-sharers of the Zamindari were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of different persons were printed. 

 Thus in the Khatians mentioned above on the front page on the top at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/ পরিচয়ে the names of Zamindars were printed and at the right hand side under the heading অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of tenants/riots were printed and at the over leafs of some of the above Khatians, the names of the possessors were printed. 

 Regarding C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contains in Ext. 4, as it appears at left hand side under the heading উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words উপরিস্ত স্বত্ব/পরিচয়ে the words ভারত সম্রাট were printed and under the heading অত্র স্বত্ব/ অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল the name of Public Works Department on behalf of Bharat Samrat, have been printed and it is only at the over leaf, Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was shown as mere possessors of 48.90 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 1 as stated earlier, in C.S. Khatian Nos. 3-7, 8, 30, 31, 32, 32 Ka 33, 34, 39; 40, 43,47, 51Ka and 51 Kha of Ext. 4 in most of the cases the Court of words of the heirs of Kumar Rabindra Narayan have been shown as Zamindars and in few cases the above court of words have been shown ryot under the heading" অত্র স্বত্বের বিস্তারিত দখল and is none of the above Khatians Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself was not shown as Zamindar or tenant. It thus appears that on 23.04.1917, when the above C.S. Khatian were finally published, Kumar Rabindra Narayan ceased hold any interest in any of the above Khatians and instead the court of wards of his heirs were shown as Zamindar and tenants. 

 Accordingly how in C.S. Khatian No. 53 as contained in Ext. 4 Kumar Rabindra Narayan could be shown as possessor and like wise how in Ext. 3 also Kumar Rabindra Narayan himself could be shown as Zamindar." 

 14. Mr. Arif failed to satisfy this court making any submission to discard aforesaid findings referring any material on record. The aforesaid findings arrived at by the last court of facts are based evidence. Since Kumer Rabindra Narayon was neither landlord nor tenant in the land recorded in Khatian No. 53 and plot No. 1 no one, claiming himself as manager of Kumer Rabindra Narayon Chowdhury, had any authority to settle the same on his behalf. He was not a person immediately under whom the tenant holds and no tenancy had been established pursuant to Ext. 1 in re sport of the suit land. 

 15. The C.S. record of right was prepared in the name Public Works Department under Bharat Samrat. Such record of right is evidence of the matter referred to in the entry and should be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. Since such presumption being a statutory one could not be taken away mere by allegation that the same is incorrect. The burden of proving that such entry in the record of right is incorrect is on the party who alleges it. In this case the plaintiffs failed to rebut the presumption by adducing evidence. The documentary evidence produced by the plaintiffs are found to be forged and fraudulent one by the Court of facts. 

 16. The plaintiffs stated that their predecessor Ashraf Ali Kazi died sometime in 1948. It has also been stated in the plaint that in 1992 the plaintiffs allegedly got the papers produced in the Court in an old box. The plaintiffs did not produce any materials in support of their claim to deal with the property, at least, from 1948 to 1992. They did not take any step to record their names in the khatian and to pay rent to the Government. It is totally unacceptable proposition' that one, who is allegedly in possession in the land and structure thereon within Dhaka City Corporation, would not take any step to record/ mutate his name in the khatian, pay rent, municipal taxes, WASA, Gas bills etc.
