full_judgment:
2. Facts in a nutshell given rise to this appeal, are that, the appellants as plaintiffs instituted the Title Suit No. 64 of 2009 before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Narayangonj impleading the respondents as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of Title for an area of 1.75 acres of land situated at 5 (five) separate plots. The plaintiffs claim an area of 53 decimals of Jand in CS plot No. 167, SA Plot No. 167, CS Khatian No. 388 in SA Khatian No. 372 under Tarabo Mouza. The land originally owned and possessed by Ayamon Nessa Bibi and her name was recorded correctly in the CS khatian. Thereafter, she transferred the said land to her 3 (three) brothers namely Sheikh Mozaffor, Sheikh Majom and Sheikh Kolomdi, vide a registered saff-kabala deed No. 2884 dated 18-1-1914 and delivered possession thereon. Thereafter, Sheikh Majom and Sheikh Kolomddi got the said land, vide an amicable partition amongst 3 (three) brothers. Thereafter, Sheikh Kolomdi died leaving behind his only son Kolom Miah as his sole heir and Sheikh Majom died leaving behind his two sons namely Jobed Ali and Toyeb Ali as his heirs and they inherited the same. Kolom Miah got an area of 18 decimals of land in CS plot No. 167 vide an amicable partition and Jobed Ali and Toyeb Ali got the rest of the property in their shaham. Thereafter, Kolom Miah transferred an area of 18 decimals of land in the CS plot No. 167 to Tayeb Ali vide a registered deed saff-kabala being No. 4192 dated 21-9-1959 and delivered possession thereon. Thereafter, Toyeb Ali transferred an area of 43 decimals along with accreted land in CS plot No.167 to the plaintiff No. 2 M/s Mahebub Company, vide 2 (two) registered saff-kabala deeds being No. 26270 and 26205, both dated 22-7-1980 and delivered possession thereon. Jabed Ali also sold an area of 20 decimals along with accreted land to the plaintiff No. 2, M/s. Mahebub Company, vide a registered saff-kabala deed No. 26206 dated 22- 7-1980 and delivered possession thereon. The plaintiff No. 2 owned and possessed an area of 53 acres of land in CS plot No. 167 and accreted land an area of 13 decimals of land in total area of 66 decimals of land in the said suit plot and he mutated his name on 18-4-1985 vide a mutation case being No. 1354 of 1981-82 and paid rent regularly to the Government. He possessed the suit land by constructing a Mill within the knowledge of everyone concern. The plaintiff claimed an area of 53 decimals of land in CS plot No. 167. 

 3. CS tenant Golami Sheikh owned and possessed an area of 39 decimals of land, in CS plot No. 166, CS khatian No. 206 under Mouza Tarabo. He died leaving behind his only son Sodu as his heir. Sodu transferred an area of 19 decimals of land to his daughter Batasi Bibi and son-in-law Abdul Aziz vide a registered heba- bil-awaj deed being No. 2084 dated 29-2-1980 and delivered possession thereon. Thereafter, Batasi Bibi and Abdul Aziz transferred the said 19 decimals of land to the plaintiff No. 1 M/s Talukder Chemicals Ltd. vide 2 (two) registered saff-kabala deed being Nos. 15636 dated 29-4- 1980 and 15741 dated 29-4-1980 and delivered possession thereon. Sodu died leaving behind his two sons namely Taher Ali and Sultan Miah, they inherited rest of 20 decimals of land in said plot and their name was recorded correctly in SA khatian No. 203. They transferred the said property to this plaintiff No. 1 M/s Talikder Chemicals Ltd. vide a registered saff-kabala deed being No. 15334 dated 26-4-1980 and delivered possession thereon. The plaintiffs mutated their name and paid rent regularly to the Government paid rent of the CS plot No. 166 till 2008. 

 5. CS tenant Golami Sheikh owned and possessed an area of 31 decimals of land in CS plot No. 173, CS Khatian No. 168. Golami Sheikh died leaving behind his only son namely Sodu @ Sadaruddin as his heir. Sodu @ Sadaruddin died leaving behind his two sons namely Taher Ali and Sultan as his heirs. During the last SA operation, an area of 31 decimals of land in CS plot No. 173 was recorded correctly in the name of Taher Ali and Sultan in SA Khatian No. 137. Thereafter, Taher Ali and Sultan transferred an area of 31 decimals of land in CS plot No. 173 vide two registered saff-kabala deeds being No. 15380 dated 26-4-1980 and the deed No. 15403 dated 28-4-1980 to the plaintiff No. 1 and delivered possession thereon. 

 6. The CS tenant Munshi Sauth owned and possessed an area of 30 decimals of land in CS plot No. 171, CS khatian No. 366. He died leaving behind his two sons namely Naymuddin and Nur Boks as his heirs. Subsequently, Naymuddin died leaving behind his only son Ajmot Ali as his heir and Nur Boks died leaving behind his two sons namely Mohammad Ali and Dudu Miah as his heirs. Ajmot Ali son of Naymuddin transferred an area of 10 decimals of land in CS plot No. 171 to Mohammad Ali son of Nur Boks vide a registered saff-kabala deed being No. 641 dated 24-2-1956 and delivered possession thereon. Dudu Miah son of Nur Boks sold out 10 decimals of land to his brother Mohammad Ali vide a registered saff-kabala deed being No. 6454 dated 09-10-1956 and delivered the possession thereon. Thereafter, Mohammad Ali transferred an area of 60 decimals of land including accreted land in CS plot No. 171 vide 2 (two) registered saff-kabala deeds being No. 14214 and deed No. 14297, both dated 17-4-1980 to the plaintiff No. 1 and delivered possession thereon. The plaintiff No. 1 mutated his name and paid rent regularly to the government. The plaintiffs obtained electricity and gas connection and installed a Mill thereon and the said mill is running for the last 30 years within the knowledge of all concern. On the 15th of January, 2009 the plaintiffs went to the local Tohsil office to pay rent and came to know that the suit land was recorded as government khas land and they refused to take rent from the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs after obtaining the RS Porchas of the said suit schedule land came to know that the suit schedule land was wrongly recorded as government khas land. The suit land is a private land according to the CS and SA record and in the RS record it was wrongly recorded in the name of the government as khas land, which creates cloud in the title of the plaintiffs and the cause of action arose on 15-1-2009, as such, they filed this instant suit against the government and prayed for a decree that the plaintiffs are the sole owner of the suit schedule properties and the suit land is not government khas land. 

 7. The defendant Nos. 1-4 entered appearance by filing a written statement denying the material allegations and claims brought in the plaint and contended, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, there is no cause of action and the suit is barred by law. During the last RS operation, an area of 0.87 acres of land in SA plot Nos. 167, 166, 172, 173 and 171, under SA khatian No. 372, 135, 137 and 350 were recorded as RS plot No. 792, 793, 801 and 797, under the No. 1 khas khatian in the name of the government. This land was diluviated in the river Sheetalakkha. During the last RS operation, the Revenue Officials after surveying the suit schedule RS plot No. 792, 793, 801 and 797, recorded the said land in the name of the government under RS khatian No. 1, without any objection from any comer and the same was finally published by the concern authority, according to the provision of 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The government owned and possessed the suit schedule land, as such, no objection was filed at the time of revisional survey in SA plot Nos. 166, 167, 172, 173 and 171 and the same was recorded as RS Khatian No. 1. The plaintiffs tried to grab the government property by creating some false and fabricated documents and filed this suit against the defendants. The government owned and possessed the suit schedule land. The plaintiffs or his predecessors never owned and possessed the suit schedule land, as such; the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. Learned Senior Advocate Mr TH Khan appearing for the appellant submits at the outset that the learned Joint District Judge, found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence, the trial Court misconstrued the case and misread the documentary evidence of the case and upon non consideration of materials on record, arrived at a wrong finding and dismissed the suit, which caused miscarriage of justice. The learned senior advocate further submits that the trial court failed to consider that the plaintiffs filed this suit for declaration of title for an area of 1.75 acres of land in 5 (five) separate plots under different khatians. The court below discussed 1 (one) plot only, which is plot No. 167 under CS khatian No. 388 out of 5 (five) suit schedule plots. The trial court did not discuss anything regarding the rest of the 4 plots of the schedule and he also failed to consider the documentary evidence as well as the oral evidence adduced by the witnesses, as such, the findings of the trial court in the impugned judgment are not tenable in the eye of law. The finding of the learned Joint District Judge that the plaintiffs failed to prove their right, title and interest in the disputed land mentioned in the CS Khatian No. 388 and CS Plot No. 167, is contrary to evidence as such not sustainable in law. The trial court's finding with regard to the Exhibit ‘১-ঙ’’ that Aymunnessa Bibi did not get any right and title in the suit plot No. 167 and she was not in possession of the suit land is erroneous. The trial court’s findings with regard to the Exhibit ‘১-জ’, the deed No.2884 dated 18-1-1914 that Sheikh Mozammel, Kolom Uddin and Mozaffor did not get any right and title over the suit land, consequently the plaintiffs did not get any right and title over the suit land is also based on misreading of the documentary evidence as such not sustainable in law. The learned Joint District Judge utterly failed to consider other documents adduced by the plaintiffs, such as the Heba-bil-awaj deed No. 2084 dated 29-4-1940 and the deed No. 15636 dated 29-4-1980, SA khatian No. 203, mutation case and rent receipts of the plaintiffs with regard to the CS plot No. 166 and the deed No. 877 dated 25-8-1980 in respect of the CS plot No. 175 and the deed No. 15380 dated 26-4-1980, deed No. 1540 dated 18-4-1980 in respect of the CS plot No. 173 and the deed No. 6456 dated 17-4-1980, in respect of CS plot No. 171. Findings and decisions of the trial court in respect of the said deeds and documents are unwarranted and not tenable because of being based on misreading and misconstruction of those documents. Although, the trial court found that the plaintiffs proved their case by adducing evidence that they are in possession of the suit land. The learned Senior Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs proved their case by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence and most of the deeds adduced by the plaintiffs were executed and registered more than 30 years before and these deeds bear the evidentiary value as per section 90 of the Evidence Act. The learned trial Judge most arbitrarily and erroneously dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs, which caused miscarriage of justice. The learned Judge also failed to consider that the defendant failed to prove their right, title and interest in the suit land, as such; the RS record was wrongly prepared and recorded in the name of the government. The CS and SA records were correctly prepared and recorded in the name of the plaintiff's predecessors. The learned advocate for the plaintiff next submits that the finding of the trial Court with regard to the Exhibit ‘১-জ’, the sale deed No. 2884 dated 18-1-1914 is a forged document because there is no plot and khatian numbers in the schedule of said deed, as such, Sheikh Moazzem, Kolomdi and Mozaffor did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land through this deed. The aforesaid findings are perverse and not sustainable in law. The learned Judge misconstrued the material evidence on record and dismissed the suit on wrong findings. He next submits that the plaintiffs after possessing the suit land, mutated the same in their name and paid rent regularly to the government and there name was recorded correctly in the record of right. The government has no right, title and interest in the suit land. The Government also hopelessly failed to prove their case and the learned Judge of the trial court with erroneous findings came to an erroneous decision and the same is liable to be set-aside. 

 12. Mr SS Sarker, learned advocate behalf of the defendant- appearing on respondent submits that the learned Joint District Judge after careful consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and other materials on record dismissed the suit of the plaintiffs. He next submits that the plaintiffs seriously failed to prove their case by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence that they have any right, title and interest in the suit schedule land. On the other hand the defendants proved their case by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence that the government has right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and the said suit land was recorded correctly in the khas khatian No. 1, according to the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 13. With a view to appreciate the submission made the learned advocates from both sides we have to consider the evidence to evaluate the extent to which each of the parties has proved their respective case and in doing so we find PW 1 Mozammel Hoque Talukder deposed on behalf of the plaintiffs as Managing Director of both the companies. He reiterated the statement made in the plaint that plaintiffs bought this suit land thereafter, they mutated the suit schedule land in their name and constructed a chemical industry with financial assistance from Janata Bank Limited and they owned and possessed the suit land for the last 30 years. On 15-1-2009 he went to Nowapara Tohsil Office to deposit rent in favour of the government, but the Revenue Officials refused to take rent and claimed the same was recorded in the name of the Government under khas khatian No. 1, after obtaining RS Porcha he came to know that the said land is wrongly recorded in the name of the government as Khas land. The suit land is recorded correctly in the name of private person-the predecessors of these plaintiffs in CS and SA Khatians. This witness produced all relevant documents; these are CS khatian Nos. 388, 206, 168, 366 and 368, SA khatian No. 203, 4 copies draft RS Khatian No. 1 and Mutation Khatian 5 copies, which marked as Exhibit 1 series. He denied that the land in SA plot No. 167, 172, 166 and 173, under SA khatian No. 372, 135, 137 and 350 were diluviated in the river Sheetalakkha, during the last RS operation the land was recorded in the name of the government without any objection, in khas khatian No. 1, as RS plot No. 792, 793, 801, 797. He denied that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit land, government possesses the same. 

 14. During cross-examination this witness deposed that he filed this suit with regard to the properties of the 5 (five) CS khatians and the owners of the suit land are different. This witness stated that Ayamon Nessa Bibi owned and possessed an area of 53 decimals of land in the suit schedule property. Thereafter, she sold the said land to her 3 (three) brother. However he cannot disclose when and where the owners of the CS plot No. 167 made amicable settlement. This witness also disclosed that the RS plot Nos. of the suit schedule lands are 798, 792, 796, 797 and 801. He denied the suggestion that he bought diluviated property. This witness disclosed that in 1981-1982, he constructed a Chemical Industry, in an area of 307 decimals of land. It was measured by an Amin and the industry surrounded by boundary wall. He denied the suggestion that he constructed the said industry in the government land. He denied the suggestion that he filed this suit to grab the government land. He denied the suggestion that he deposed falsely in this suit. He also denied the suggestion that the sale deed mentioned in the plaint are false, fabricated and collusive and the vendors are not owner of the suit land. 

 19. D.W. 1 Md Solimullah, a Revenue Officer of the Tarabo Land Office, he deposed on behalf of the defendant No.1 to 4. This witness reiterated the statement made in the written statement and deposed that the suit schedule land situated in RS khatian No.1, RS plot No. 792,793, 801 and 797, SA khatian No. 372, 137, 150 SA plot No. 166, 167, 172, 173 and 179, under Tarabo Mouza. A part of the suit schedule land were diluviated in the river as such, it was recorded in the name of the government No. 1 khas khatian, an area of 20 decimals of land in RS plot No. 792, an area of 13 decimals of land in plot 801, 31 decimals of land in plot No. 797 and 18 decimals of land in plot No. 793. In total an area of 87 decimals of land were recorded in the No. 1 khas khatian. The said 87 decimals of land belonged to the government. This witness deposed that the government possessed the suit land. He denied the suggestion that the plaintiffs possessed the suit schedule land. This witness produced all relevant documents; these are attested photocopy of SA and RS khatian, which marked as Exhibit 'ka' series. 

 21. These are all about the deposition of the witnesses in a nutshell wherefrom it transpires that the plaintiffs filed this suit for declaration of title for an area of 1.75 acres of land in 5 (five) separate plots under different khatians, including an area of 53 decimals of land in CS Plot No. 167 under CS Khatian No. 388. The land originally belonged to one Ayamon Nessa Bibi, she transferred the suit land to her 3 (three) brothers namely Sheikh Mozaffor, Sheikh Majom and Sheikh Kolomdi vide a registered saff-kabala deed being No. 2884 dated 18-1-1914, the said deed is exhibited as Exhibtit '১-জ-'. 

 22. We have noticed that the findings of the learned Joint District Judge with regard to the CS Khatian No. 388 and the registered saff-kabala deed No. 2884 dated 18-1-1914 that Ayamon Nessa Bibi did not acquire any right, title and interest according to the CS Khatian No. 388, as such, Sheikh Mozaffor, Sheikh Majom and Sheikh Kolomddi did not acquire any right, title and interest in the CS plot No.167 vide registered saff-kabala deed being No. 2884 dated 18-1-1914. Firstly, the trial court finds that Ayamon Nessa Bibi could not prove her right, title and interest in an area of 53 decimals of land in CS plot No. 167, under CS Khatian No. 388. In this regard the learned Joint District Judge observed that: 

 23. We have perused the CS Khatian No. 388, in the plain reading of this CS khatian, we find that the name of Aymon Nessa Bibi appeared as owner of the suit land and the name of one Mofizuddin appeared as korfa (under-raiyet), an under-raiyet or cultivating raiyet, who holds land by cultivating it either by himself or with the aid of some other person, he was not owner of the said land. Further, Ayamon Nessa Bibi transferred the suit land in 1914, long before enactment of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The aforesaid findings of the trial court with regard to the Exhibit '1-P' that Aymunnessa Bibi did not get any right and title in the suit plot No. 167 and she was not in possession of the suit land was erroneous, unjust and not sustainable in law. It was recorded correctly in the name of Ayamon Nessa Bibi and which established her right, title and possession in the suit plot No. 167, under CS khatian No. 388. As such, we find and hold that the findings of the learned Joint District Judge with regard to the CS khatian No. 388 is erroneous, wrong and misconstrued. 

 25. Learned Joint District Judge disbelieved this registered saff-kabala deed No. 2884 dated 18-1-1914, assigning a reason that there is no plot and khatian numbers in the said deed. We have perused the aforesaid deed, which marked as Exhibit > (), we find that it is an ancient document. In the schedule of said deed the land was described by the boundaries, it was butted and bounded at the eastern side jote of Golami, at the southern side the jote of Munshi soud, at the western side the Lakka river and at northern side the jote of Kadir Boks and Rahim Boks. However, the operation of Cadastral Survey in our country was started in 1890 from Chittagong and it was finished in 1940, in Dinajpur District. The sale deed was executed and registered in 1914, during this period people and the deed writers used to identify or specify land, by the owner of surrounding jote etc. as well as the measurement of the land. We do not find any wrong in describing or specifying the land in the sale deed by names of the owners of the surrounding jote, as the plot numbers were not available at that time. 

 26. Further, where any document purporting or proved to be 30 years old is produced from the proper custody, section 90 of the Evidence Act entitles the court to presume that it is a genuine document. The deed itself is more than 30 years old is an ancient document. A 30 years old document when produced from proper custody presumption under section 90 of the Evidence Act as to its validity can be raised. Learned Joint District Judge utterly failed to consider the CS record as well as this ancient document and came to a wrong finding that the plaintiff's predecessors-in-interest do not have any right and interest in the suit land. 

 27. On a careful scrutiny of the judgment of the trial court we find that the learned Judge of the trial court failed to consider that the plaintiffs filed this suit for declaration of title for an area of 1.75 acres of land in (five) separate plots under different khatians. From the materials placed before us and the evidence on records including the exhibits, we find that the learned Joint District Judge did not consider other 4 (four) CS plots mentioned in the schedule of the plaint, though the plaintiffs adduced oral and documentary evidence in support of their case. The trial court utterly failed to consider other documents of the plaintiffs, which were testified by the PW 2 and PW 3 such as, (a) the Heba-bil-awaj deed No. 2084 dated 29-4-1940, the deed No. 15636 dated 29-4-1980, the deed No. 15741 dated 29-4-1980 and 15334 dated 26-4-1980, SA khatian No. 203, mutation case and rent receipt of the plaintiffs with regard to the CS plot No. 166, (b) the deed No. 15248 dated 25-4-1980, mutation case and rent receipt of the plaintiffs with regard to the CS plot No. 172, (c) registered saff-kabala deed No. 15380 dated 26-4-1980 and the deed No. 15403 dated 28-4-1980, SA Khatian No. 137 mutation case and rent receipt of the plaintiffs with regard to the CS plot No. 173, CS Khatian No. 168. (d) the deed No. 641 dated 24-2-1956, deed No. 6454 dated 09-10-1956, deeds No. 14214 and deed No. 14297, both dated 17-4-1980 mutation case and rent receipt of the plaintiffs with regard to the CS plot No. 171, CS khatian No. 366. 

 29. On a careful scrutiny of the judgment of the trial court we find that the trial court was of the opinion that that defendant failed to prove that the suit schedule land was acquired by the Government through the process of alluvion and diluvion. In respect of finding to this effect, we have also scrutinised the evidence and find no reason to differ with the learned Joint District Judge in respect of this finding. We have also noticed that the trial court was of the opinion that the plaintiff successfully proved that they possessed the suit land by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence. However, we have noticed that the learned Joint District Judge found to the effect that the plaintiff failed to prove their title in the suit land. From the material placed before us and the consideration of the evidence on record, we | find that plaintiffs produced all relevant documents and oral evidence to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and their names were recorded correctly in the CS and SA Khatians. The RS record was wrongly prepared and recorded in the name of Government under khas khatian at the instance of a vested quarter.

full_judgment:
3. The case of plaintiffs is that, suit land originally belongs to Bhawal Raj. The suit land of schedule 'Ka' comprising of an area of 23.13 acres of land recorded in CS khatian No. 7 along with other lands in the name of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Chowdhury settled the suit land in raiyati right. On the death of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, his heirs as of tenanted right was owner in possession of the entire land of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As per Court of Wards Act 1879, the management and administration of the property including "Ka" schedule land of CS khatian No.  7 was taken over by the Court of Wards. During the last CS record, it was recorded in the name of Court of Wards, for Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others, which was subsequently named as Bhawal Raj Courts of Wards Estate or Bhawal Court of Wards Estate or Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate. Bhawal Court of Wards Estate as owner and possessor of `Ka' schedule land with other lands of CS khatian No.  7, settled 'Ka' schedule land with the father and husband of the plaintiff. Bashoruddin and co-sharer, Chand Mia through its own printed pattannama. Basiruddin and Chand Mia became owner and possessor in equal share. While Basiruddin and Chand Mia on the basis of pattannama and dakhila and by paying zamindari taxes to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate, the Government, then province of East Pakistan by giving effect of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act acquired the rent receiving interest of the Zaminder and on taking nominal taxes as land development tax, the tenants were classified as owner of their respective land as per sections 3 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. After acquisition of the rent receiving interest as aforesaid, Government published final gazette as per provision of section 3 of the aforesaid Act on 24-3-1952. After acquisition of the land as aforesaid, Compensation Assessment Roll were prepared and Zaminder as per the aforesaid compensation assessment roll received compensation and gazette was published on 29-5-1956 as per section 42 of the aforesaid Act by which the Zamindari of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury of `Ka' schedule land, was acquired and the status of tenant. Basiruddin and Chand Mia were changed and become owners. Accordingly SA khatian was finally published in their names. By opening jote in the revenue office and by paying nominal land development tax possessing the suit land SA khatian No.  63 was finally published in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia in equal 8 annas share. Basiruddin and Chand Mia upon an amicable settlement partitioned the kha schedule land by which 'Ka' schedule land fallen in the saham of Basiruddin. After acquisition of the land by the Government, 5.40 acres of land remain in the hand of Basiruddin alone which has been mentioned in 'Kha' schedule. Chand Mia got 'Ga' schedule land which comprising of 0.39 acres of land of dag No. 155/1061, 0.51 acres of land of dag No. 1059, 1.42 acres of land of dag No. 1063, 1.18 acres of land of dag No. 1058, 0.60 acres of land of dag No. 1060, in total, 4.10 acres of land and remaining land, in total 13.36 acres including 12.5 as mentioned in 'Gha' schedule was in ejmlali and co-sharers as owners owned and possessed by cultivation. While the aforesaid land was in possession of co-sharers, 1.48 acres of land was acquired by the Government out of 13.63 acres of land for road and remaining land i.e. 12.15 acres of land, "Gha' schedule, was in ejmali of the co-sharers. While co-sharers as aforesaid was in possession having title there to, Government acquired portion of land for defendant No. 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, defendant No. 17, Rice Research Institution from the land of Chand Mia to the very knowledge of defendant No.  1 and 14 in LA Case No.  100/65-66, recognizing Chand Mia as the owner of the aforesaid land. Compensation was received by Chand Mia while in possession, 12.15 acres of land described in schedule `Gha', constructed homestead, planted trees and cultivated agricultural lands in ejmali, died leaving, defendant No.  6 as heir who along with other co-sharers possessing the land in ejmali. While defendant No. 6, plaintiff and Chand Mia was in possession of the ejmali property of 'Gha' schedule comprising 12.15 acres, Government in LA case No.  5/85-86 acquired 10 acres of land for defendant No.  19, Gazipur District Police Line under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs. In LA Case No.  3/2001-2002 Government acquired 0.33 acres of land for defendant No.  26, District Fisheries Officer under defendant No.  25, Ministry of Fisheries and Veterinaries under Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  7/90-91 acquired 0.09 acres of land for defendant No. 20, District Jail, Gazipur under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs, in LA Case No.  3/95-96 acquired 0.33 acres of land for Defendant No.  District primary Education office under defendant No. 21 Ministry of Education, Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  5/90-91 acquired .50 acres of land for defendant No.  24, Public Health Engineering Department under defendant No.  23, Ministry of Health, Government of Bangladesh. Government disbursed compensation money part of the afore-said 5 LA cases to the plaintiffs and to the co-sharers having found they are legal title holder. Some greedy person of the locality created obstruction in getting compensation money and gave proposal to defendant No. 6, son of defendant No. 9 and brother of defendant Nos.  1 and 8, but recognized their title over 'Kha' schedule land when they would manage in getting the compensation money to the plaintiffs. Later on, Chand Mia died leaving defendant Nos.  2-5 as heirs. Plaintiffs, the heirs of Chand Mia, defendant Nos. 2-5 are waiting for getting compensation money. Suddenly, on 12-12-2007 the manager of defendant No. 14 and the officer of Bhawal Court of Wards came to 'Kha' schedule land whereupon plaintiff could know that defendant No. 1 of the instant suit along with defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 filed in the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur against defendant Nos. 3-6, in total against 11 persons as defendants and they got decree. Defendant No. 1 of the instant suit got decree up to the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. In RS record 18.70 acres of land of 'Kha' schedule recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 and they requested plaintiffs to give up possession of the suit land. Defendant No.  1 of the instant suit threatened plaintiff that if they did not give up possession to the defendant No.  14 amicably then they by force evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land. Plaintiffs went to defendant No.  14 to know about the decree, then, the manager of defendant No.  14, Abdur Rouf, gave a paper book to plaintiff No.  1 and requested plaintiff No.  1 to go through paper book to find out how the suit was decreed. Plaintiffs after getting paper book asked defendant Nos.  6 and 3 as to how they got decree in the suit to which they kept silence. Defendant No. 1 with connivance with defendant Nos.  6-13 got the decree surreptitiously. 

 5. It is further case of plaintiffs that, defendant Nos.  1 to 14 in connivance with the employees of Deputy Commissioner turned the relevant portions of SA khatian which was kept in the record room of Deputy Commissioner but the said SA khatian having been kept in other offices like tahsil, AC Land office including DG, DLR office of the Government wherein the said SA khatian with index is found and on scrutinizing of SA khatian No.  63 it appears that said SA khatian No.  63 was prepared in the name of predecessor of Basiruddin and Chand Mia and on the basis of said SA record the other document i.e. for collection of the rent, i.e. talab baki register which is retisger-2 and from Union land office, earlier Tohsil Office it is seen the record stand, in the name of plaintiffs predecessor and in index in different LA Cases, wherein on the basis of said SA khatian No.  63, lands were acquired and compensation money were disbursed in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia. It is seen that the aforesaid khatian was prepared in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia. 

 6. It is further case of plaintiffs that during final survey prior to RS record, recorded the name of plaintiffs but employees of survey settlement department recorded otherwise in finally published RS khatian. On the basis of the aforesaid SA khatian No. 63, Government acquired land for defendant No.  17, Bangladesh Rice Research Institute and also for other Government machineries. The aforesaid RS khatian No. 506 was prepared wrongly in the name of defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho in the name of Shebayet of Deity Sarju Bala in 8 annas share and in the name of Bivabati Devi, wife of, Kumar Ramcendra Narayan Ray Chowdhury in 8 annas share whose name had not been recorded in CS as well as SA khatian. 

 10. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 is that, suit land was recorded in CS khatian Nos.  7 and 770 ultimately in RS khatian No.  506 and 1011 and quantum of land was 23.13. Original owner of the suit property was Kumar Rabindra Narayant Roy Chowdhury and others and later, Bhawal Court of Wards. While Chowdhuries were in possession, they installed family deity as Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho and puja expenses were paid from their own income. The aforesaid Bhawal Raj for maintaining the deity for worship, handed over their entire property to Bhawal Court of Wards under Court of Wards Act, 1879 and from 1911 Court of Wards maintained the case property on behalf of Bhawal Raj Estate. CS record recorded the name of Court of Wards on behalf of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and other co-sharers. Bhawal Raj maintained the Estate by giving barga and adi Barga, maintained possession, Vz portion of the crops was given to the manager and remaining 1A portion to the cultivator. Manager as shebayet, by the income worshiping the family deity. The name of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is correctly recorded in RS khatian. Suits were filed for and against Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho and decree was passed in favour of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho. The case of plaintiffs is false. 

 12. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that Gha schedule of the suit land has been acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 100/65-66, LA Case Nos.  5/85-86, 5/90-91, 3/ 95-96, 3/2001-2002 and 7/90-91 giving compensation money to the plaintiffs and his co-sharers. In SA khatian No. 63,23.13 decimals of land recorded in the name of Basiruddin in 8 annas share. In RS khatian No.  506,18/3 acres of land has been recorded in the name of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho in 8 annas share. The Government has no claim excepting the land which has been acquired by the Government where Government has title. 

 17. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff appellants, submits that, pattannama exhibit-2 was disbelieved by the learned Judge on the ground that dates mentioned therein in Bengali has no similarity with the corresponding English date without properly going through the contents thereof as the date in Bengali mentioned in the middle side of the pattannama is the preliminary date of pattan subject to the approval of the Chief Manager and the date in English after signature of the concerned Nayeb of Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate is the date after approval of the pattan by the Chief Manager of the said Court of Wards. Learned Advocate further submits that judgment passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and also of those of the higher Courts up to the Appellate Division wherein decision arrived are not supported by law as the lands of SA Khaian No.  63 of the suit land was settled as pr6jabili and as per President Order No. 90 of 1972 no suit can be filed against the lands settled as projabili as such said judgment having passed on wrong assumption of law affirmed up to Appellate Division is a judgment per in curium. Learned Advocate submits that rent receipts were granted by the Zaminder and thereafter, by the Revenue Authority of the Government after whole sale acquisition of the land and on the face of such legal position, preparation of RS khatian in the name of defendant No. 1 is without any basis, the court below without considering the materials on record abruptly hold pattanana as forged which finding is erroneous in as much as the names of Basiruddin and Chand Mia was duly recorded in the subsequent documents like Register II, the Talab Baki Register, exhibit-5, Compensation Assessment Roll, exhibit-8, rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit-4 and lastly in SA khatian, record of right after effecting the 'projapattani'. Learned Advocate further submits that document filed connecting with projapattani being more than 30 years old and has been produced from proper custody of the plaintiff-appellants got presumptive value of its execution and further submits that learned Judge committed gross illegality in holding that SA khatian produced form, the side of plaintiffs is a created document upon using a revenue stamp and bears no signature of Officer-in-Charge of record room is baseless and against the record and also against order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 passed by the learned Judge on the application filed by the plaintiffs for calling the record from the Revenue Department whereupon the court ordered that since Government produced SA khatian as such record from Revenue Department is not required to be called to settle the dispute without considering that Government produced distorted SA khatian. Learned Advocate further submits that the findings of the learned Judge that in Title Suit No. 12 of 1976 it is decided Chand Mia is a bargadar under defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is baseless and fully on surmise and conjecture as the contesting defendant-respondent No. 1 and 14 who claimed their title through those judgments, had neither filed nor exhibited those judgment in the present suit as such finding of the learned Judge that Chand Mia had admitted in those previous suits that he was a bargadar is baseless and full of surmise and conjecture not supported by any law. Learned Advocate further submits that court below was in erroneous findings of fact as it should have considered the vital documents like the rent receiving interest acquisition gazettes, exhibit Nos. 7 and 9, written statements of defendant Nos.  6 to 32, true copy of the SA khatian produced by the Government, exhibit No.  `Kha; the register No. II i.e. Talab Baki Register, exhibit No. 5, Compensation Assessment Roll exhibit No. 8 and the rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit No. 4, which are although in certified copies are not challenged by the Government while marked as exhibits and non-consideration of those vital documents led the Court below to erroneous finding as to the title of the plaintiffs-appellants. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs-appellants from the time of pattan upto the date of forceful eviction on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 has been proved by the oral and documentary evidences of the plaintiffs-appellants and also by the defendant's witnesses, DW 1 and DW 2, learned Judge committed gross illegality in not declaring title of the plaintiffs over the suit property by adverse possession. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs have been proved through municipal tax receipts, electric and gas bills, house rent receipts etc. exhibit 13 series and also Advocate Commissioner's report and such non-consideration of those vital documents as to possession of the plaintiffs led the Court to an erroneous finding as to title of the plaintiffs, as possession follows title. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No.  1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho having not been represented by the Shebayet in the previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 2985 as plaintiff and in the subsequent present Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  14 the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate having no connection with the deity, has no locus standi to file the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 and also to contest the subsequent Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as its representative, so, the decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and the dismissal decree passed in Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 is illegal and without jurisdiction. Learned Advocate further submits that neither defendant No. 1 nor defendant No.  14 filed any document of acquiring title in the suit property nor proved their possession therein, but the learned trial court dismissed the suit on coming to the conclusion on surmise that the defendant No. 1 is a owner of the suit property. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 14 having admitted that all the properties except ‘Kha' schedule property have been acquired by the Government and also compensation have been paid to the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 for recovery of khas possession of the entire 18.73 acres of land including the acquired land, is illegal and not binding upon the persons in possession through acquisition. 

 21. The aforesaid points taken up for consideration may be summarized as to whether i) the 'Kha' schedule 5.40 acre suit property and other 18.73 acre property total 23.13 acre property recorded in the admitted CS khatian No.  7 was a projabili property under the jamindar, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Ray Chowdhury represented by Court of Wards and as to whether ii) the plaintiffs appellants' predecessor, Bosar Uddin and his co-sharer Chand Miah were projas under the said judgment or that the defendant No. 1 Sree Sree Madab Bigraha was the proja under the said jamindar and lasty as to whether iii) the lower court below is correct in dismissing the suit by impugned judgment. 

 42. Plaintiffs case is that they got pattern of the land from Zaminder of Bhawal and since then they are in possession, at first, under the Zaminder and later on, under the Government until dispossess in 2008. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 2 is that property having belongs to a deity, this property could not be alienated by anyone except legal necessity; RS khatian prepared rightly, plaintiffs title has been extinguished and defendant No. 1 having got decree in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 this suit was dismissed rightly. The case of defendant No.  6 is that he was not a party to Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 as he did not appeared in the suit and his father's name was not rightly recorded. It is the case of defendant No.  6 that defendant No. 1 had no title nor possession and on the basis of decree of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 defendant Nos.  1 and 14 illegally threatened plaintiffs from dispossession from the suit land. Defendant Nos.  6-17 wants saham for 4.10 acres of land which has been acquired for Bangladesh Rice Research Institute. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that the suit land has been acquired from plaintiffs by different LA Cases and suit land has been rightly recorded in the name of plaintiffs and SA, khatian No. 63 in 8 annas equal share to Basiruddin, predecessor of the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, predecessor of the defendant Nos.  2 and 6. 

 43. It appears that Government in written statement admitted plaintiffs are the owner of the suit property as in the written statement Government stated that in different LA Cases Government acquired land from plaintiffs and from their co-sharer and SA Khatian No.  63 was rightly prepared in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and also of his co-sharer, Chand Mia and it is also the case of the Government that plaintiff of Title Suit No 1219 of 1985 and defendant No.  1 of the instant suit has no title or possession. As such, title of the plaintiffs has well established. On this background let us refer to the depositions of the witnesses particularly of defendant's witnesses who stated as:— 

 48. This pattannama has been acted upon as from exhibit-3 series it appears that the pat-tan holder paid Zaminderi tax up to 1942 then from exhibit No. 4, dakhila, it appears land has been recorded as 'projabili' extinguishing title of Superior landlord, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. From exhibit No.  2-4 it appears from the column of the khatian that name of plaintiffs and co-sharer have been recorded for 23.13 acres of land as projabili. Exhibt-5 is Talib Baki Register-II kept in the custody of Government where also we find the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs from whom tax was collected. Exhibit-6 series are rent receipts stand in the name of plaintiffs and their predecessor. Up to this plaintiffs have been able to prove that they have paid rent to the Zaminder pursuant to the pattan taken from Zaminder i.e. up to 1952. 

 52. Exhibit-11 official document, a notice, issued as per section 3 for acquiring the land by the Additional land Acquisition Officer, Gazipur to Chand Mia and also to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. This document goes to show continued possession of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land. In front of all these government documents RS khatian was published in the name of defendant No. 1 showing Surjabala Debi and Bibhabatibala Debi, wife of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury as possessor in 8 annas share each is totally baseless. It is admitted position that RS khatian was prepared in between 1969-1985. 

 54. Bhawal Raj is known to all of Bangladesh for many reasons including the famous case of Mejo Kumar and Bhibaboti Debi. For this reason family of Bhwal Raj is well known to all of us. It is also known that Bhibaboti Bala Debi as well Surjabala Debi left this country (East Bengal) just after pronouncement of judgment in 1919, as such, in 1985 their names cannot appear as possessors in the RS khatian, as such, it can be definitely said that RS khatian has been prepared illegally without any basis. 

 63. Now, as to the basis of SA khatian. 

 64. From the side of defendant No. 1 it appears that attested copy of SA khatian No.  63 was produced exhibit 'Ka' and RS khatian No.  506. Learned Judge disbelieved SA khatian exhibit 1 submitted by plaintiff as it is not tallied with the certified copy of the SA khatian produced from the side of defendant No.  1. We are of the view that learned Judge was totally on wrong premises as plaintiff not only produced certified copy but also in their statement stated that this SA khatian can be found from different departments of government and also from the Government and filed application for calling for the volume from concern Assistant Commissioner (land) of Gazipur whereupon the court passed order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 as:— 

 65. The SA khatian exhibit-la' submitted from the government custody and the SA khatian submitted from the plaintiffs custody, exhibit -1 are of the same and the same was recorded in the joint names of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin citing them as owners of the 'Ka' schedule suit property in equal II, anas owner each. From the judgment of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985, it is found that the present defendant No.  1 Deity had submitted SA Khatian No.  63 before the court claiming to have recorded in its name as owner. But here in this case, he with-held the said SA khatian and had submitted an information slip exhibit 'kha(1)1 stating that the SA khatian remained in the record room of DC office was turned of for the reason best known to him without explaing whatsoever about the previous exhibited SA khatian No.  63 in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985. In such circumstances, it can easily be concluded that since the attested true copy of the SA khatian No.  63, exhibit-'Ka" submitted from the government custody and since the government had admitted in their written statements that the SA khatian No.  63 was prepared and published in the joint names of than Miah and Basor Uddin in equal share and since the said SA khatian exhibit `Ka' and the SA khatian of the plaintiffs, exhibit-1 are of the same and since the SA khatian prepared in the name of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin has got the basis i.e. exhibits-4 to 9, the plea of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 that the SA khatian was prepared in the name of defendant No.  1 is forged and fraudulent is not correct finding, rather we can come to the conclusion that the SA khatian, exhibit-1 was duly and correctly prepared and published in the name of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Moreover, the finding of the previous suit regarding SA khatian prepared in the name of Chan Mian and plaintiffs' predecessor Basor Uddin is not binding upon the plaintiffs as the present plainiffs were not party in the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985. 

 66. As such it may be reasonably presumed that defendant No.  1 intentionally produce distorted certified copy of SA khatian which learned Judge failed to consider and the finding of the learned Judge is totally beyond pleading of the parties. 

 70. Now, if we scrutinize the RS khatian No.  506, exhibit-12, we finds that same was recorded in the name of “ শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ সেবাইত দং সুরুজ বালা দেবী। বিভাবতি দেবী। জং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী সাং নিজ।” The self same RS khatian was also filed by the defendant Nos.  1 and 14 claiming to have been correctly prepared and published in the name of defendant No.  1, Bigraha marking the same as exhibit Ka(1). In this respect the DW-1, Assistant Manager, Court of Wards of Bhawal Raj Estate stated in his deposition as follows:— 

 71. From the aforesaid statements made in cross-examination it is found that the DW-1 at one time claims that the 'Ka' schedule property is owned by the Court of Wards and at another time claims that the suit property is owned by the Deity, the defendant No.  1. At one stage, the DW-1 admitted that it had no basis for recording the name of Deity in the RS khatian. The two woman Shebayets as cited in the RS khatian had left the then East Pakistan now Bangladesh before Division of Pakistan and India. So the RS record prepared and published in the name of defendant Nod, Bigraha represented by two women as shebayets in equal II. Eight anas share as possessors is admittedly baseless and without foundation and, as such, the plaintiffs-appellants are entitled to have the relief against the said RS record as prayed for in his plaint as wrong, illegal, without any basis and not binding upon the plaintiffs appellants. 

 76. Learned Judge on the question of SA khatian No.  63 holds that it cannot be relied but we find that defendant No.  1 produced SA khatian and to overcome said SA khatian, plaintiff filed application for calling volume for the concerned Assistant Commissioner (Land) office but court rejected the said application as such statement of the learned Deputy Attorney-General has no leg to stand. 

 82. Thus we are of the view that the leave petitioner had no locus-standi to challenge the draft Mahanagar Survey Khatian as prepared in the name of the respective writ petitioners, at-least after publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956." learned Advocate next relied on the case of 14 MLR (AD) 401 where it is held that "The plaintiffs were never recognized as co-sharers and on the contrary the heirs of Jinnat Ali are in exclusive possession of the suit land since the time of the CS record and they have acquired good title by continuous adverse possession for over 12 years. The right title interest of the plaintiff and their predecessor to the suit land has been extinguished by ouster and hostile adverse possession." Learned Advocate on adverse possession relied on 13 MLR (AD) 329 where it is held that "The plaintiff-respondent who embraced Islam is found to have been in peaceful and uninterrupted possession adversely to the interest of all others for more than 12 years and thereby acquired good and indefeasible title to the suit property described in schedule B of the paint which was formerly their family debattar property. The family Deity was removed there from and consequently the suit property ceased to be debattar property. The High Court Division set-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and restored the judgment and decree of the trial court on the above findings which the apex court held perfectly justified. 

 92. From the aforesaid facts, evidences both oral and documentary and also law involved in the case we conclude that the entire 23.13 acre `Ka' schedule property was a probability property before SAT Act. 1950. So, the said 23.13 acre 'Ka' schedule property was duly recorded in the names of the then projas namely Chan Mian and Basaruddin in SA Khatian No.  63 (Exhibit-1) by operation of section 3 of the SAT Act, through publishing probability property Gazette (Exhibit-7) and also by PO 90 of 1972 the RS Khatian No.  506(Exhibit-12) recorded in the name of  শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ সেবাইত দং সুরুজ বালা দেবী। বিভাবতি দেবী। জং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী সাং নিজ।” is baseless and without foundation, as such, the same is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The defendant No.  14, Court of Wards, Bhowal Raj Estate claiming as shebaiyet of defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  15, Land Reform board had illegally evicted the plaintiffs appellants on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 from the `Kha' schedule property violating the order of injunction passed by the High Court Division on 3-3-2008 in Civil Rule No.  132(FM) of 2008 and also during the pendency of Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 of the joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur and as such, the plaintiffs are entitled to recover the said dispossessed 'Kha(2)' schedule property as prayed for in their petition dated 10-7-2008. The plaintiffs appellants having proved their right, title and possession in the rest of the 'Kha' schedule property i.e, `Kha(1); 'Kha(3); 'Kha(4); 'Kha(5)' and Kha 6 schedule property are entitled to protect their said property by the decree of confirmation of possession and permanent injunction.

full_judgment:
2. Respondent nos. 1 and 2 instituted the above suit seeking declaration of title of 2.385 acres of land appertaining to S. A. khatian Nos. 635 and 629, corresponding to R. S. khatian Nos. 1 and 418 of mouja Kaunia respectively as described in the schedule to the plaint. Plaint case in short is that the suit lands appertaining to C. S. khatian no. 8 under khebot No. 248 were equally owned and possessed by three brothers namely, Kali Das Dhupi, Raj Kumar Dhupi and Gurudas Dhupi as restless Karsha Service tenants under Houla landlord Osman Kha and others. Rajkumar Dhupi died unmarried leaving two brothers Kalidas Dhupi and Gurudas Dhupi. Thereafter, Gurudas died leaving only son Prasanna Kumar Dhupi, on whose death, the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 and 2 became his successor sons. On the other hand, Kalidas Dhupi leaving only son Mahesh Chandra Dhupi, on whose death, his four sons namely Satish Chandra Dhupi (defendant no.1), Rajendra Chandra Dhupi (Predecessor of defendants no. 2-5, Shashi Chandra Dhupi (Predecessors of defendants no. 7 and 8) and Haridas Dhupi (Predecessor of defendant Nos. 8-10), and the R.S. and S.A. khatians in the name of Mahesh Chandra Dhupi in exclusion of prasanna and his heirs were wrong and in-spite of wrong records, the plaintiffs maintained ejmali possession of the eight annas share of the disputed jamas, but as the defendants denied their title , they filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant-petitioner no.4 contested the suit by filing a written statement which was adopted by the defendants no. 1, 2-5. His case in short is that original service tenant Nasai Dhupi held the jamas as service tenure under landlord Dhircndra Krishna Mukhapadhaya and subsequently got the same recorded in the names of his three sons namely Rajkumar, Gurudas and Kalidas and after such record Raj Kumar and Gurudas left their private service as was Herman of the landlords and Kalidas alone continued his service as was Herman of the Zaminders and under such circumstances, Kalidas died leaving his son Mahesh Chandra Dhupi who exclusively continued possession of the suit jama and got his name recorded in R.S. and S.A. khatians and thereafter, Mohcsh as exclusive owner and possessor of the suit jamas died leaving four sons and the defendant nos. 1-10 are the admit-ted successive heirs of Mahesh Chandra Dhupi and thus he pleaded correctness of the R.S. and S.A. khatians in the name of his predecessor Mahesh Chandra Dhupi and denied plaintiffs title and possession in the suit land and stated that non-suited holdings were his paternal properties acquired otherwise. 

 6. Mr. M. M. Abdul Quayum, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in affirming the judgment and order of the Court of appeal below in failing to consider that the trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record found exclusive possession of the defendants in the suit lands since the time of preparation of R. S. khatian which has a presumptive value but the Court of appeal below without reversing those findings of possession decreed the suit. Learned counsel further contended that the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to advert to the point involved in the suit that in view of the provision of sections 89 and 181 of the Bengal Tenancy Act, the plaintiffs can not acquire any title in the suit lands. The trial Court on a proper appreciation of the evidence on record held that the plaintiffs failed to prove that their predecessor Prasanna ever served the Landlords to justify their claim, that the defendants proved that their predecessor Mohesh Chandra held the tenancy serving as private servant of landlords, that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession and that the suit is barred by limitation. On the other hand, the Court of appeal below did not reverse all those findings on proper appreciation of the evidence on record, and learned Single Judge of the High Court Division has affirmed the judgment of the court of appeal below in failing to consider that the court of appeal below has not reversed of the findings of the trial court while decreeing the suit. 

 7. The points raised by the learned counsel merit consideration. Leave is therefore granted to consider the following points: "(II)Because the High Court Division committed error of law in not considering that the trial court found actual exclusive possession of the land of suit jamas with the defendants which finding was not reversed by the appellate court, but the High Court Division erroneously by making a fresh appreciation only of oral evidences found possession of the plain-tiffs disregarding the vital evidences of D.Ws. 2-5 and presumption of possession available under finally published R. S. and S. A. khatians along' with up-to dated real receipts and series of registered deeds Exhibit D series since 1961 produced by the defendants, (III) Because the High Court Division committed error of law in not overriding the appellate court findings on the issue of title in the premises of provisions of sections 89 and 181 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and in the light of reported age old decisions of the superior courts as regards incidents of service tenancy distinguished from occupancy rights of other tenants."

full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 34 of 1989 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Munshiganj, for declaration of title and for khas possession. The plaintiff's case in short is that one Kademunnessa Khatun was the superior landlord of the suit land and Salim Khan, Alep Khan and Fazil Khan, sons of Baru Khan, were bargadars under the said landlord and the same has been correctly recorded in the CS Khatian. Afterwards, the said bargadars handed over the said lands to the Zamindar's Seresta. Abdur Razzak, the son of the said Kademunnessa sold out lands in the suit plot No. 42 to Shamsuddin Bhuiyan alias Raja Mia, father of the plaintiff appellants, by registered sale deed dated 19-12-1942 and delivered possession thereof and later Abdul Kashem Sona Mia and Golam Saber Shamsuddin Ahmed grandsons of Kademunnessa became owner-possessors of suit plot No. 41 on basis of a gift and while thus they were owning and possessing the same, they sold out the said land of Plot No. 41 to aforesaid Shamsuddin Bhuiyan and at the relevant time vendor Golam Saber Shamsuddin Ahmed being minor, the patta deed dated 1-7-1944 was executed and registered by his father, the natural guardian, and accordingly said Shamsuddin Bhuiyan has been possessing as owner of the suit plots and enjoying usufructs therefrom on payment of rates and taxes to the Sheresta of the Zaminder and, after withdrawal of the Zamindari System, said Shamsuddin Bhuiyan became a tenant directly under the government pursuant to the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, was owning and possessing the suit lands on payment of rates and taxes to the government and that in the SA Khatian, along with the name of Shamsuddin Bhuiyan wrongly the names of aforesaid Salim, Alep and Fazil Khan appeared, and that said Salim, Alep and Fazil Khan did never claimed ownership or possession on the suit plots and they did not pay any rents ever to the government in respect of the suit land. After the death of Shamsuddin Bhuiyan and his wife Rahima Begum, their three sons, the plaintiffs, and one daughter inherited the properties left, including the suit land and on amicable partition, amongst themselves, the plaintiffs got the suit land in their saham and thus became the exclusive owner-possessors of the suit land and were enjoying usufructs there from through Bargader, since they were in employment at different places, and that the plaintiff No. 1 on his retirement, is possessing the suit land and cultivating the same with his own men and that on 9-8-1987 the defendant No. 1, taking advantage of the wrong recording of the names of said Salim Khan and others in the SA Khatian along with real owner Shamsuddin Bhuiyan, claimed the suit land alleging inter alia that father of the defendant No. 1 Abdul Jabbar on 18-3-1984 purchased the suit land from the heirs the SA recorded tenants namely Salim Khan and his two brothers and threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land and that faced with such situation the plaintiffs filed criminal case in the Court of Magistrate, who upon hearing dismissed the case holding the defendant to be in possession of the suit land and that the plaintiff also lost in the appeal filed against the order passed by the Magistrate, however as per observation made by the appellate Court, the plaintiffs filed the suit. The defendant contested the suit denying ownership and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land relying on purchase made by his father. The plaintiffs adduced four (4) witnesses and produced documents marked Exhibits-1 to 4 series in support of their case and the defendant adduced five (5) witnesses and produced documents marked Ka to Gha series in support of his case Five (5) issues were framed and the suit was dismissed holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land as well as their story of dispossession from the suit land. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 107 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge, Munshiganj, which on transfer was heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge allowing the appeal and setting-aside the decree passed by the trial Court and thereby decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 22-3-1997 declaring the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land and ordered for recovery of khas possession and that the defendant-respondents being aggrieved moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1480 of 1997 and Rule issued therein was heard and disposed of by the judgment and order discharging the Rule, which has been impugned in his leave petition. 

 "Mr Md Shafiqul Islam Dhali the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite-party in reply submits that the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, firstly committed error of law in misreading the Exhibit 3, registered deed of sale dated 1-8-1989 executed by CS recorded Zamindar Akkas Uddin in favour of Hazetun Nessa transferring the rent receiving interest of the suit land along with other land, inasmuch as, the same being a registered deed of sale executed and registered about 90 years old and negative presumption of the same could only be formed through evidence keeping in view of the development and circumstances consequent to the execution and registration thereof till the present. Mr. Dhali next submits that the plaintiffs exhibited as many as 20 rent receipts out of them some were issued by Zaminder and 18 of them issued by the Government, being Exhibit 4 series proved the payment of rent in respect of the suit land till 1988 by the plaintiff and also proved the possession and enjoyment of the suit property by the plaintiffs and further standing of collateral evidence of title of the plaintiffs in support of his contention, but the learned Sub-ordinate Judge in his judgment mentioned that the plaintiffs exhibited only 2 rent receipt and thereby proceeded towards by the erroneous decision in support of his contention Mr Dhali relies on the decision of our. Appellate Division reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216 wherein it has been held that rent receipts through not documents of title, are not items of evidence of possession and may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows of title. Mr Dhali further submits that SA Khatian being Exhibits Kha(2) and Kha(3) and RS Khatian finally published being recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively although one of the two SA Khatian being Exhibit Kha(2) contained the name of the CS recorded tenants along with the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff. In this connection Mr Dhali submits that it is settled principle of law that the last record of right will prevail than the earlier record of right, in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 35 DLR 295 and 17 DLR 392 and 27 DLR 589 relying on the decision of a Division Bench of this Court reported in 42 DLR 434. Mr Dhali submits that RS Khatian prepared under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has the presumption of correctness under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Mr Dhali finally submits that although the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge is not lengthy but the learned Additional District Judge refers the Judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge adverting the material findings of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and discussed the oral and documentary evidence in doing so and that there is no misreading of any evidence on record and neither there is any non-consideration of material evidence on record on the part of the learned Additional District Judge and that being so the Additional District Judge being appellate Court and thereby being the final Court of facts, its judgment is not liable to be interfered with." 

 And thus found that the trial Court arrived at its wrong decision because of non-consideration of the material evidences on record, namely the rent receipts granted by the government marked Exhibits-4 series and the deed dated 1-8-1899, a 90 years old registered deed as well as the SA Khatian and RS Khatian, standing in names of the predecessor-in-interest and in the name of the plaintiffs respectively, marked Exhibits-Kha(2) and Kha(3). We do not find any reason of differ with the same.
