parties:
Kamakshya Ranjan Haider and ors ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Prafullya Kumar Haider & others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. Plaintiffs' case, in short is, that the suit lands along with other lands appertained to RS khatian No. 21 measuring an area of 12.95 acres belonged to Rajmohon, Ketu and Panchu. Rajmohon had 4.27 acres of land in his share and on his death, his 8 sons Kailash, Rasik, Rojoni, Surjokanto, Rakhal, Piyari and Choto inherited their respective shares. Ketu died unmarried while he was jointly residing with his brother Rajmohon leaving wife Feli and nephew Kailash Chandra. During his lifetime Ketu executed a registered will in respect of his share of land giving 12 annas share to Kailash Chandra and 4 annas share to his wife Feli, specifically pointing out that on her demise Kailash would inherit the entire lands. Accordingly, after the death of Feli, Kailash got Ketu's share of 4.27 acres and inherited 0.59 acres as son of Rajmohan. Jogesh Chandra being the only son of Kailash inherited the said lands but in the RS khatian 4 annas share was wrongly recorded in his name though he had 6 annas share. Panchu died leaving two sons, Kanai Lal and Kalicharan @ Khoka but in the RS and SA khatians more shares than they were legally entitled to were recorded in their names. Jogesh Chandra transferred 1.34 acres of land out of his 4.86 acres by registered kabala dated 19th August 1957 in favour of the plaintiff No. 1, his mother Maloti and the plaintiff No. 4. On the same day, Jogesh also transferred 1.34 acres of land by another deed in favour of the plaintiffs-predecessors Kaishore, Mohananda and Satish. Kalicharan @ Khoka exchanged 0.84 acres of land by a registered deed dated 2nd June 1958 with plaintiffs-predecessors Mohananda, Kaishore and Satish out of his inherited property and in pursuance of that exchange, the plaintiffs-predecessors got lands in Shakhari Kati mouja and Kalicharan got lands in the suit Gaokhali mouja. Mohananda died leaving no issue and accordingly Kaishore inherited his share and on the death of Kaishore, the plaintiffs Nos. 1-3 got his share. Satish also died leaving no issue while residing jointly with his sister Maloti and accordingly, the plaintiffs Nos. 1-3 got his share as well. In this way the plaintiffs are claiming title in respect of 1.84 acres of land. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. According to them, in the suit khatian Rajmohon, Ketu and Panchu had 13.13 acres of land and accordingly, each brother had 4.38 acres of land. Rajmohon died leaving 8 sons and each son inherited 0.49½ acres of land. Ketu died leaving no issue and therefore, his brother Panchu Ram inherited his share. In the premises, Panchu had 8.75 acres of land from his share and as reversionary heir of Ketu. Out of 13.13 acres of land, 1.16 acres were settled to the tenants and therefore, Rajmohon, Panchu and Ketu had  11.79 acres of land and accordingly, Panchu Ram in fact had 7.86 acres and after his death, Kanai and Kalicharan, his two sons, inherited the lands. Kanai died leaving 4 sons, Judhusthir, Nittyananda, Gouranga and Narayan. They by 5 registered deeds transferred 3.93 acres of land in favour of defendant No. 3. They claimed that although the RS record was incorrect but their title was not clouded and that the deed of exchange was forged, collusive and the plaintiffs did not acquire any title on the basis of those deeds. 

 5. Admittedly, the petitioners are the co-sharers in the suit khatian. According to the plaintiffs, they have title in respect of 1.84 acres of land in the suit khatian as described in schedule 'ga' to the plaint. On the other hand, the defendant admitted that the plaintiffs are entitled to only 0.49½ acres of land as their predecessor Kailash did not get the share of Ketu and that Ketu's brother Panchu, the defendants' predecessor, inherited his share. Therefore, the main controversy in this suit is, who has inherited share of Ketu? The learned Joint District Judge observed that the record of 4(four) annas share in RS khatian No. 21 (Exhibit 1) in Kailash's name proved that besides inheritance, Kailash got lands from other source and as a result, the RS khatian was prepared. He further observed that the RS khatian did not prove that Kanai and Kalicharan, sons of Panchu, inherited 7.86 acres of land from his father and from the share of Ketu, inasmuch as, in the said khatian Panchu's 1/3rd share was recorded in their names that proved that Punchu did not get Ketu's share. The trial Court further held that plaintiffs' predecessors purchased 2.68 acres of land out of 4.86 acres by two deeds dated 19th August, 1957 (Exhibits 4 and 5) from Jogesh, son of Kailash and after they exchanged 0.84 acres of land from the suit Mouja with Kalicharan, the plaintiffs had 1.84 acres of land in the suit khatian after excluding 0.84 acres, which is the disputed 'ga' schedule lands. By the deeds of exchange the plaintiffs predecessors got 0.84 acres of lands from Shakhari Kathi Mouja and Kalicharan got 0.84 acres of land from the suit Mouja (Exhibits 6 and 6(ka). He further held that Exhibit 2 indicated that Mohananda, Lalit, Adityo and Dwijabor, were sons of Jagabandhu Haider that proved that Mohananda had three full brothers, and thus, in presence of full brothers, Kaishore being the cousin of Mohananda did not inherit Mahananda's share. In view of the above, the trial Court came to the conclusion that Mohamanda had 0.4475 acres of land out of 1.34 acres he along with his brothers acquired by purchase jointly by kabala dated 19th August 1957 (Exhibit 5) from Jogesh, that as the plaintiffs failed to prove that they inherited the share of Mohananda, they were entitled to 2.2325 acres after deducting 0.4475 acres of Mohananda's share, and that out of that lands their predecessors Kaishsore, Mohananda and Satish exchanged 0.84 acres of land with Kalicharan on 10th June 1958, (Exhibit 6(ka)) and thus, they have title in respect of 1.3925 (2.2325-0.84) acres of land in schedule 'ga'. 

 6. The trial Court further held that on the death of Panchu his two sons Kanai and Kalicharan inherited 2.135 acres each and on the death of Kanai, his sons Judisthir, Nittyananda, Gouranga and Narayan acquired title of 2.135 acres and not 3.93 acres, that the defendant No. 3 failed to produce title deeds that his predecessors Judisthir, Nittananda, Gouranga and Narayan had title in respect of 3.93 acres of land, that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 being the heirs of Kalicharan inherited 2.135 acres of land and therefore, they are entitled to 2.135 acres of land and that the RS khatian proved that Panchu's sons, Kanailal and Kalicharan have inherited his 1/3rd share. 

 7. The lower appellate Court observed that in the remark column of RS khatian only 0.70 acres of land was shown in the possession of Kailash and other co-sharers were in possession of other plots, that on the basis of such possession 7.96 acres of land was recorded in the corresponding SA Khatian No. 39, in the names of Kanailal and Kalicharan, and 0.70 acres of land in the name of Jogesh in khatian No. 213 and that these khatians proved that despite mentioning 4 annas share in the khatian Kailash was in possession of only 0.70 acres of land. These findings of the Court of appeal below are based upon hypothesis, inasmuch as if Kailash did not get the share of Ketu on the basis of will, there was no reason for recording /4/ annas share in his name in Exhibit-1. His share in the lands of RS khatian would have been equal with his other seven brothers. The Court of appeal below without assigning any reason observed that Kailash was not in possession on the basis of the record which finding is in conflict with earlier finding. The Court of appeal below also did not reverse the findings of the trial Court that this recording in the khatian proved that Kailash got other lands apart from his father Rajmohan. Plaintiffs claimed that this record of /4/ annas share was due to mistake but, in fact, he was entitled to /6/ annas share on the basis of the registered deed of will dated 17th February, 1913 (Exhibit-7). 

 8. In the RS khatian (Exhibit 1) 3 annas and odd i.e. 1/3rd share, was recorded in the names of Kanai and Kalicharan, the predecessors of the defendants. The trial Court on consideration of this khatian, rightly held that the RS record did not support the claim of the defendants that Panchu inherited the share of Ketu and that after the death of Panchu, his sons Kanailal and Kalicharan did not inherit the share of Panchu. The lower appellate Court did not at all consider these findings of the trial Court and on a superficial consideration of the khatians held that the RS khatian supported the defendants' claim. The Court of appeal below failed to consider that the defendants had knowledge about the recording of /4/ share in the name of Kailash but their explanation was that despite such record, their title was not clouded; they however, failed to substantiate their claim. They have not challenged the RS khatian at any point of time which has presumptive value. 

 9. Mr Abdul Quayum, learned Advocate, fails to explain the basis of recording /4/ annas share in the name of Kailash and the basis for recording 7.96 acres of laud in the SA khatian in the name of defendants' predecessors. Learned Advocate, however, contends that though in the RS khatian less share has been recorded in the names of Kanailal and Kalicharan than they were legally entitled to, the SA khatian has been correctly prepared as they have inherited Ketu's share. This submission of the learned Advocate is the reiteration of the defendants' claim but the defendants have adduced no legal evidence in support of their claim, other than the SA khatian, The recitals in the will disprove their claim. 

 11. An amendment in the plaint is allowed for determining the real question in controversy between the parties and once an amendment of the plaint is allowed the amendment will relate back to the date of the institution of the suit and will be operative from that date. The defendants did not challenge the amendment in the plaint and the Court of appeal below, in the premises, erred in law in disputing the plaintiffs' claim only because those facts were not pleaded in the original plaint. The Court of appeal below fell in an error in failing to appreciate that no particular form is necessary in executing a will. It is sufficient if it contains the testamentary wishes of the deceased; the reference in this connection is sections 377 and 378 of the Hindu Law. A will is the legal declaration of the intention of a testator with respect to his property which he desires to be carried into effect after his death. Primarily, the words of the will are to be considered. They convey the expression of the stator's wishes. In Exhibit 7 the testator stated that on his demise, his wife Feli and nephew Kailash would enjoy his property in /4/ and /12/ annas share respectively and that on the death of his wife, Kailash would get her share as well. It is a registered instrument and executed on 17th February, 1913, more than 86 years prior to its filing in Court on 23rd November, 1999 by the plaintiffs from their custody claiming that Kailash got Ketu's share in the khatian on the strength of this will. It being a document of more than 30 years old produced from the proper custody, the Court may presume that (a) the signature and every other part of it which purports to be in the handwriting of the scribe is in that person's' handwriting, (b) the will was executed by Ketu, and (c) the will was attested by the persons by whom it purported to have been attested under section 90 of the Evidence Act. There is also presumption that the will was prepared at the time it was purported to have been prepared. The Court of appeal below has totally ignored this legal aspect of the matter while considering the will, Exhibit 7. 

 12. The finding of the Court of appeal below that this will has not been acted upon in the absence of the probate of the will is also based upon misconception of law. Apart from the legal position, there are sufficient documentary evidence on record suggesting that this will has been acted upon. In the RS khatiar (Exhibit 1) 4 annas share was recorded in the name of Kailash and if the will had not been acted upon, his share would have been shown equal with his other brothers. Exhibit-6 proved that Kaishore, Mohananda and Satish exchanged 0.84 acres of land by registered deed of exchange with Kalicharan alias Khoka, son of Panchu out of 1.34 acres of land which they purchased from Jogesh son of Kailash by registered kabala dated 19th August 1957 (Exhibit 5). By this deed of exchange (Exhibit 6) Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish got lands from Shakhari Kati Mouja and Kali Charan got lands from the suit Mouja Goakhali (Exhibit 6(ka)). Kalicharan, the predecessor of the defendants acknowledged the title of Kaishore, Mohananda and Satish, who had got those lands from Jogesh. Kailash inherited only 0.59 acres from the share of Rajmohan according to the plaintiffs, and according to the defendants. he inherited only 0.49-1/3 acres bu this son Jogesh had transferred 1.34 acres of land by Exhibit 5 out of the suit khatian. Therefore, unless the deeds, Exhibits 5 and 7, were acted upon, Kalicharan would not have exchanged lands. Therefore, there is no doubt that the will was acted upon, and the defendants predecessor had acknowledged the acquiring of Kailash's title on the strength of the will, and that these deeds of will and exchange being old registered instruments have presumptive value in the absence of contrary evidence. 

 13. The Court of appeal below misread the RS khatian and observed that the RS khatian No. 21 and SA khatian No. 39 (Exhibit Kha and Kha(1)) proved that 7.96 acres of land were recorded in the names of Kanailal and Kalicharan, sons of Panchu Rain. In RS khatian (Exhibit Kha) which corresponds to Exhibit-1, only 3 annas and odd share has been recorded in the names of Kanailal and Kalicharan. In the SA Khatian 7.96 acres of lands were recorded in their names but in view of the above findings I find no basis of this record. There is no presumptive value of SA Khatian and the defendants-opposite panties have failed to show the basis of recording lands as such. The Court of appeal below disbelieved the plaintiffs claim of transfer of 1.34 +1.34 acres of land by Jogesh by registered kabalas dated 19th August, 1957 (Exhibits 4 and 5) in favour of Kamakkha Ranjan, the plaintiff No. 1, Malati Rani, mother of plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and Laxmi Rani, the plaintiff No. 4, and Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish respectively on the reasonings that Exhibit 4 was a certified copy, which the deed was entered in Volume No. 2770, but they did not call for the original volume for reception of secondary evidence and that the dag, khatian numbers and the areas of the lands in these deeds were identical. 

 14. The Court of appeal below was of the view that the deeds were created by the predecessor of the plaintiffs Kaishore Chandra for which the original deed (Exhibit 4) was not produced. The Court of appeal below failed to notice that Exhibit 4 was admitted into evidence without any objection and out of 1.34 acres lands transferred by Jogesh in favour of Kaishore, Mohananda and Satish (Exhibit 5), Kalicharan got 0.84 acres by way of exchange from Kaishore, Mohananda and Satish (Exhibit 6 ka). The registration number of Exhibit 4 is 2776 and it was registered in registration book No. 1 at pages 13-15. It was executed by Jogesh in favour of Kamakkah, Maloti and Laxmi Rani. Whereas, Exhibit 5, is registered deed No. 2777 and the said deed was executed by Jogesh in favour of Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish. This deed was entered in registration book No. 1 at pages 16-19. These facts prove that these deeds have been executed simultaneously and that the recipients of these deeds are distinct persons, and also in respect of separate lands out of the total area of 12.95 acres in the khatian. Therefore, there is no doubt that by these deeds different lands have been transferred to different sets of persons out of the same plot. The Court of appeal below on a superficial consideration of these two deeds observed that these deeds were collusively created by Kaishore Chandra. 

 15. As observed above, Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish, jointly on one side, and Kalicharan on the other exchanged suit plots No. 2209, 2210 and 2213 of Mouja Gaokhali with the lands of mouja Shakharkati of plot Nos. 1557, 2040, 2005, 20089, 2234, 2204, 2205 and 2208 by executing two registered deeds. The Court of appeal below found fault in the deeds on the reasonings that the second parties in those deeds did not put their signatures and that Exhibit 6(ka) was a certified copy. The Court of appeal below failed to notice that the parties did not execute one deed of exchange, rather they executed two deeds and in their respective deeds they put their signatures. The deeds were very old instruments executed on 10th June 1958 and there was reference in Exhibit '6' about Exhibit 6(ka), the original of which was lying with the defendants predecessor as he was the recipients of the lands. In Exhibit 6(ka) Kalicharan acknowledged the title of Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish in respect of 0.84 acres of land of suit plots No. 2209, 2210 and 2213, who got the said lands from Jogesh by kabala dated 19th August, 1957 (Exhibit 5). The defendants simply said that this deed of exchange was collusive but they did not lead any evidence in support of their claim of collusion. This is a registered deed and this deed proved that the deed of will was acted upon and by dint of this will, Kailash got Ketu's share, and after his death, Jogeshinherited the same and thereafter, Jogesh transferred the same to Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish and thereafter, Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish exchanged three plots with Kalicharan. The lands of Shakharkati mouja have been recorded in RS khatian No. 17 (Exhibit 2). Since Khoka @ Kali-charan acknowledged the title of Kaishore, Mahananda and Satish, the Court of appeal below erred in law in holding that this deed of exchange was a collusive one. 

 16. The Court of appeal below on a misreading of the evidence on record disbelieved the plaintiffs' possession. In support of plaintiffs' possession, they examined 3 witnesses, of them, PW 1 Kamakkha Ranjan Haider stated that he along with other plaintiffs have been possessing 1.84 acres of land in RS khatian No. 21 excluding 0.84 acres of land and also other lands in RS khatian No. 17. In cross-examination, he said that they have been possessing 2.68 acres of land in plots No. 2208, 2209, 2210 and 2213. PW 2 Motaleb Bepari stated that he has been borga cultivating 0.74 acres of land in plot No. 2208, and 1.14 acres in plot No. 2209. The Court of appeal below observed that PW 2 did not corroborate the plaintiffs claim in the plaint. This witness deposed about the lands he was borga cultivating on behalf of the plaintiffs. He was not deposing on behalf of the plaintiffs in respect of their entire lands. The Court of appeal below also disbelieved PW 3 Abdul Latif Miah observing that though he deposed in support of plaintiffs' possession but in course of cross-examination he failed to say the boundary of the suit lands. The Court of appeal below misread his evidence. He stated in course of cross-examination that "মামলার জমির চৌহদ্দী বলতে পারব" He did not say that he could not say the boundary of the suit lands. 

 17. Apart from the oral evidence, the defendants also admitted the plaintiffs' title and possession at least in respect of 0.49-1/2 acres of land. They did not altogether deny the plaintiffs' title in the suit lands. The plaintiffs are admitted co-sharers in the khatian. Admittedly the suit lands remain in ejmali and in view of the observations of the appellate Court about the maintainability of the suit, the plaintiffs filed an application for amendment of the plaint seeking partition and the application was allowed.

The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 1, 3, 22, 24, 26 and 42-47 by filing joint written statement denying the material averments made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that Aminuddin son of Khoaj owned and possessed the land of C.S. Khatian No. 87 and 124 were required to be prepared in the name of Aminuddin, Jamiruddin and Yasin but Aminuddin in collusion with the survey officials got the land recorded in his name alone, that Aminuddin inspite of record of right prepared in his name never claimed more than 1/3rd share in the land of C.S. In total Gedu Miah sold 18¼ decimals of land and thus exhausted his entire share, that Yasin died leaving 3 sons, Abdul Motalib, Abdul Hamid and Abdul Karim and one daugher Tahera and they possessed the land left by Yasin in ejmali and they purchased 2 decimals of land from Shukur Mahmud, that Abdul Motalib died leaving defendant Nos. 2-10, that Abdul Karim, plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 2-10, used to live in the homestead of Yasin, that in Yasin's portions plaintiffs, defendant Nos. 2-10 and defendant No.1 have huts of different size, that in Khoaj's part his heirs are living. 

 6. As against the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court the contesting defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that by the kabala Ext. 3 Abdul Motalib and Rahima Khatun did not acquire any title in the land of S.A. full_judgment:
3. The petitioners filed the above suit praying for partition after declaration of their title in the suit land contending, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to C.S Khatian No. 117 measuring 2.01 acres originally belonged to Sharbananda Das and Matinath Das in equal shares and their names were recorded in the C.S. Khatian and out. of the above 2.01 acres of land one decimal of land was acquired for the road; Sharbananda, who got 1.00 acre of land in his share, he died leaving behind one daughter the defendant No.1 and one son the plaintiff No.2, the plaintiff No.1 was possessing the suit land as her life estate; that plaintiffs have homestead in the western side of Plot No. 227 and they, without partition, were facing inconvenience to possess the suit land and hence the suit for partition. The defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to C.S, Khatian No. 116 is under Khatian No. 117; Sarbananda Das and Matinath Das were the korfa tenants of the suit land and they having defaulted in paying the Rent Suit No. 3485 of 1940 was filed which being decreed Rent Execution Case No. 807 of 1941 was filed in which Purnamayee, the mother of defendant No.1 auction purchased the same on 10.9.1941 and got possession; Purnamayee being in possession of the suit land since her auction purchase S.A. Khatian was prepared in her name and she duly paid rents and after her death her son, the defendant No.1 is in possession of the same and the plaintiffs were no longer in possession of the suit land after the auction sale. 

 4. The trial court decreed the suit in preliminary from holding that suit land appertains to C.S. Khatian No. 117 and both parties admitted that Sarbananda and Motinath Das were the tenants in the said C.S. Khatian No. 117; Sarbananda was predecessor of the plaintiffs and Motinath was the predecessor of the defendant No.1; the lands of C.S. Khatian No. 117 were not auction  sold and the defendants could not prove that Purnamayee, the mother of the defendant No.1, got the land of C.S. Khatian No. 117 on the basis of auction purchase and as such preparation of S.A. Khatian in the name of Purnamayee has no basis at all; the documents filed by the defendants show that it is only the lands of C.S. Khatian No. 116 which were auction sold and as such plaintiffs title and possession in respect of eight annas share in respect C.S. Khatian No. 117 as described in the schedule Ka of the plaint being proved the plaintiffs are entitled to get a preliminary decree. 

 5. The defendant No.1 then preferred Other Class Appeal No. 31 of 1995 and the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Kurigram, after hearing, allowed the appeal holding that the certified copy of the C.S. Khatain No.116 shows that C.S Khatian No. 117 is an under tenure Khatian of C.S. Khatian No. 116 and so after the lands of C.S Khatian No. 116 were auction sold the title and possession of the Korfa tenants under C.S. Khatian No. 117, which is the under tenure Khatian of C.S Khatian No. 116, automatically extinguished; the trial Court ought to have found that Poyatu Barman was the tenant of C.S. Khatian No. 116 and Sarbananda and Motinath were the korfa tenants of C.S. Khatian No. 117 which is the under tenure Khatian of C.S Khatian No. 116; according to the provisions of section 48(C) of the Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 if the land of tenant is auction sold, the possession of korfa tenant is extinguished and so after such auction sale there is no necessity to file any case against korfa tenants after issuing any notice upon them, the plaintiff No. 1 claimed portion of the suit lands on the basis of her life estate and if her claim is accepted then how her son, plaintiff No.2, during her life time can get the land as per provisions of the Hindu Law. The plaintiffs then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in civil Revision 1815 of 1999 and the High Court Division after hearing discharged the Rule holding that admittedly the suit land appertains to C.S. Khatian No. 117 and the total land in the Khatian is 2.01 acres and Sarbananda and Motinath were the korfa tenant under Puyatu Barman and Harakanta Barman in equal sharers, the C.S. Khatian No.117 has been marked exhibit Ka(1); Exhibit Ka is the C.S. Khatian No. 116 in which it is found that C.S. Khatian No. 117 was the under khatian of khatian No. 116 as such 2.01 acres of land was also mentioned in that khatian; the papers and evidences filed show that 2.01 acres of land was auctioned sold in Rent Execution Case No. 807 of 1941 and Purnamoyee auctioned purchased the same through Court and Ext. Gha is the sale certificate showing the area of auctioned land as 2.01 acres; Ext. Ga is the S.A. Khatian where the name of Purnamoyee has been recorded in respect of the land auction purchased by her and there are good number of rent receipts which has been marked exhibit Kha series showing payment of rent by Purnamoyee which prove the continuous possession of the defendant No.1; the plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses among them P.W.1 is the plaintiff No. 2 the son of plaintiff No.1 and P.Ws.2 and 3 are the neighbours and P.W.4 is the plaintiff No.1, the mother of plaintiff Nos. 2; P.W.4, in her cross-examination stated that she does not know whether the suit land has been auctioned sold or not and she is also not aware of the S.A. record of the suit land; she never paid rent of the suit land and can not say the khatian and plot number of the suit land and her son has instituted the suit; the above statement of P.W.4 on oath goes against the case of plaintiff as she herself did not file the suit and it is only her son, plaintiff No.2, instituted the present suit during the life time of his mother and so plaintiff No.2, has no locus standi to file the suit. The High Court Division in its judgment referred to the case of Rai Krishna Shaha vs. Md. Matleb Ali Pramanik and others reported in 34 DLR (HCD) 179 where it has been held:-

full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff is that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 1 of Mouza Darigachha under P.S. and District-Bogra originally belonged to landlord Bimalendu Roy Bahadur. During C.S. operation, the land was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 1 in his name. But in the remarks column of the Khatian the suit land was written as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” Actually, the local people had no possession in, or prescriptive right over the suit land as such, the recital “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” in the remarks column of the C.S. Khatian was wrong and illegal. 

 7. Defendant Nos. 13 and 14 filed another written statement. Their case is that the land of plot No. 794 is a tank and that plot No. 2446 measuring 7.07 is a part of River Bhadai, used by the local people. Since there is no embankment of the tank, the local people use the water of the tank for irrigation from the time of their forefathers. Accordingly, in the remarks column of the C.S  khatian, the suit land was shown “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” By practicing fraud upon the local authority and suppressing the rec9rd containing the entry “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land. 

 15. Having perused C.S. khatian No. 1 of Mouza Darigacha, I find that plot No. 794 was shown as tank and in its remarks column, the tank was shown as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” Chapter 111 of the Government State Manual, 1958 gives detailed descriptions of the Register that is to be maintained. According to Rule 22, Register VIII is a register of unoccupied lands and will be maintained in parts: 

 16. From the above rule, it appears that water tanks used by public cannot be leased out. In the case in hand, we find that in violation of the above rule, the land of plot No. 794 was leased out to the plaintiff. It is, however, contended that in the remarks column of C.S. record through mistake it was written “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. In this connection, it is important to note here that according to section 103 B (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, every entry made in a record-of-rights shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. The plaintiff, how-ever, could not rebut the presumption of correctness of the entry made in the C.S. khatian including the entry made in its remarks column in which it was written “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. 

 In the present case the land was recorded in the C.S. record as well as S.A. Khatian as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. As the public had rights in the disputed land, the settlement made in favour of the plaintiff was not legally done, and by the impugned orders such settlement was correctly cancelled by the revenue authorities."

Vs.

full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiff-petitioners, in brief, is that the plaintiff-petitioners filed Title Suit No. 18 of 1996 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Damudya, Shariatpur for declaration of title to the suit land and for declaration that the recent survey record in the name of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 instead of the names of the plaintiffs alone in respect of the suit land is illegal and without any basis and for permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 from entering into the suit land and from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land alleging, inter alia, that 5.72 acres of land in different plots under C.S. Khatian No. 99 of Purba Kandi mouza within P.S. Goshairhat was owned and possessed by Miah Chand Chowkidar. He died leaving behind his only son Bahar Ali @ Bahar Ali Chowkidar, only daughter, Joygun Bibi and wife Miajan Bibi. Bahar Ali Chowkidar, as per his share, while possessing in the suit land sold out .44 decimals of land of plot No. 666 under schedule I by kabala, dated 11.10.23 to Shafizuddin Sarder, Abe predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs. The said land was duly recorded in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs in R. S.Khatian No. 187 as plot No. 469. In the title column of B.S. Khatian, the name of the heirs of Mia Chand Chowkidar and Shafizuddin Sarder and others are seen. Though their names were recorded but in the remark column of the said record, possession in respect of the suit plot was shown in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs. In the last S.A. operation the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs was recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 210 in- ejmali with Babu Kha and defendant No. 1 in respect of 3.83 acres of land where the name of the plaintiffs' predecessor was also shown alone in the possession column against the suit plot and that does mean that plaintiffs predecessor -in-interest used to possess the suit plot exclusively. While the predecessor of the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession in the suit plot he sold out .11 decimals of land out of the suit plot to Abdur Rahim Sarder, son of Abdul Hashem Sarder, by kabala dated 1.4.1976 and handed over possession to him who then sold out the same to one Delwara Begum. Thereafter Delwara Begum sold out her said purchased land to plaintiff No. 4 by kabala dated 19.4.1987 and he has been possessing the same since then. Shafizuddin Sarder died leaving behind sons , plaintiff Nos. 1-3 as his heirs , thus the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land within the knowledge of the defendants and general people for more than 12 years. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land, in collusion with the employees engaged for survey records, illegally got the suit land recorded in their names with the plaintiffs in the recent Khatian. On the basis of the said illegal and wrong record, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the last part of Ashar , 1404 B.S. threatened the plaintiffs with forcible dispossession from the suit land and hence the suit. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the land under suit Khatian was owned and possessed by Joygun Bibi and Mohammad Bepari who sold 1.28 acres of land out of the suit, khatian including the land of C.S. Plot No. 666 in favour of Shafizuddin, the predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and Babu Kha and Chamol Bibi, the father and mother of the defendant No. 1 and handed over possession to them. Thereafter Bahar Ali Chowkidar sold out 1.62 1/2 acres of land out of the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 99 by registered deed dated 1.1.1944 to Shafizuddin, predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and defendant No. 1 and his father Babu Kha. The S.A. Khatian No. 210 was rightly recorded in respect of the suit land in 1/3 share in the names of Shafizuddin Sarder, Babu Kha and Jobbor Kha each. Thereafter defendant No. 1 sold out some land out of the suit land to the defendant No. 2. The present hal record in respect of the suit land has been prepared correctly. The suit land being an ejmali property, the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any relief as prayed for without asking for partition and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 7. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing the parties without considering the points involved in the case reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court holding that the trial court had erred in law in decreeing the suit declaring the title of the plaintiffs to the suit land which appertains to an ejmali Khatian and as such without seeking for partition simple suit for declaration is not maintainable. 

 10. Mr. A.B. Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners submits that the land of the previous suit jote measuring 5.72 acres appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 99 (Ext. 1) previously belonged to one Miajan @ Mia Chan Chowkidar who died leaving wife Manijan Bibi, son Bahar Ali Chowkidar and daughter Joygun Bibi and then Manijan Bibi died leaving Bahar Ali Chowkidar and Joygun Bibi as son and daughter respectively . He further submits that Bahar Ali Chowkidar, while he had been exclusively possessing .44 acres of land appertaining to R.S. Plot No. 469 out of the suit land sold out that 44 decimals of land by kabala in the year 1923 ( Ext.7) to Shafizuddin Sarder, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs and in R.S. Khatian No. 187(Ext.2) which was admittedly prepared and published during 1942 to 1948 under the provision of Bengal Tenancy Act and that in Ext. 2 Shfizuddin Sarder's possession by purchase was recorded in .44 decimals of land appertaining to R.S. Suit Plot No. 469. He further submits that the plaintiffs' predecessor Shafizuddin had been possessing the suit land since 1923 and after him the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land and thereby acquired valid title thereto but the Court of Appeal below failed to appreciate that aspect of the matter as well as the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the plaintiffs and thereby arrived at an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice which caused serious prejudice to the plaintiff-petitioners. 

 11. Admittedly, the original suit jote measuring 5.72 acres of land including the suit land measuring .44 acres of land of B.R.S Plot No. 1088 corresponding to C.S. Plot No. 666 and R. S and S.A. Plot No. 469 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 99 (Ext. 1 ) previously belonged to one Miajan @ Miachand Chowkidar and he died leaving wife Manijan, son Bahar Ali and daughter, Joygun Bibi and Manijan died leaving Bahar Ali Chowkidar and Joygun Bibi as son and daughter respectively. It is also an admitted fact that Bahar Ali thereafter sold out .44 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No. 666 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 99 to one Shafizuddin Sarder, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs by a registered deed in the year, 1923 A.D. (Ext. 7). The R.S. Khatian No. 187, marked Ext. 2, corresponding to C.S. Khatian No. 99 shows that the lands of the original suit jote with an area of 5.75 acres were recorded in the names of the riyots with their specific share in the jote and in the "remark column" it is mentioned that the plot No. 469 with an area of .44 decimals was being possessed by one Shafizuddin Sarder son of Tither Ali Sarder on the basis of purchase. In Ext. 2, against all other plots, names of the respective possessors were also mentioned showing their respective share in each of the pion. Ext. 3 is the S. A. Khatian No, 210 which relates to 3.83 acres of land including the suit land measuring .44 decimals of plot No. 469 wherein against suit plot No. 469 exclusive possession of Shafiz Ali @ Shafizuddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs has been mentioned in its entire .44 decimals of land. Rent receipt Ext. 5 shows that An Sarder (plaintiff No. 1) son of Shafizuddin paid rent for the suit land in respect of Plot No. 469 appertaining to Khatian No. 210 upto 1397 B.S. The BRS Khatian No. 282 marked Ext. 6 shows that this khatian stands prepared exclusively in respect of only suit Plot No. 1088 with an area of 44 decimals which is admitted to have been finally published in the meantime. Ext. 6 appears to have been recorded in the names of both the plaintiffs and the defendants. Plaintiffs asserted through a registered deed executed in the year 1923 marked Ext. 7 that by this deed Bahar Ali Chowkidar, who had admittedly 2/3rd share in the original suit' jote, sold out 44 decimals of land in R.S. Plot No. 469 corresponding to C.S. Plot No. 666 which has subsequently been transformed into BRS plot No. 1088 to Shafizuddin Sirder, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs . From R.S. Khatian, marked as Ext. 2, it appears that the share of all the co-sharer-tenants has been specifically mentioned therein against their names along with their individual and specific possession in each plot of the jote wherein in 'remark column' exclusive possession of Shafizuddin Sarder predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs in .44 decimals of land of R.S. Plot No. 469, on the basis of purchase, stands mentioned: The facts dis-closed in the Ext. 2 give rise to presumption that there was at amicable partition amongst the co-sharers of the C.S. jote before the preparation of the R.S. record which reflects in the R.S. Khatian No. 187 (Ext. 2). Had there been no such amicable partition the specific share of each of the co-sharer tenants with their specific possession along with specific possession of the transferees from them in each individual plot of the suit jote would not reflect in R.S. Khatian (Ext. 2). In S.A. Khatian No. 210, marked. Ext. 3, too the exclusive possession of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs has been mentioned in .44 decimals of land of Plot No. 469. 

 13. The R.S. Khatian No. 187, marked Ext. 2 and S.A. Khatian No. 210 marked Ext. 3 show that exclusive possession of the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs was mentioned therein over .44 decimals of land of suit plot No. 469 amongst other plots of the khatian belonging to other co-sharers. In view of the facts, circumstances and evidence as referred to above it appears that the plaintiff-petitioners have been able to make out a good case than the case of the defendant-opposite parties. 

 14. In S.A Khatian No. 210 (Ext. 3) the exclusive possession of -the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs in the suit land measuring 44 decimals of land in plot No. 469 has been mentioned . Thereafter the BRS khatian No. 282 marked Ext. 6 has been prepared exclusively in respect of only one plot, i.e., the suit plot No. 1088 which corresponds to A.S. and S.A. Plot No. 469 and C.S. Plot No. 666 measuring .44 decimals of land. Ext. 6 has been prepared in the names of both the plain-tiffs and the defendants. In view of Ext. 6 it is apparent that co-sharership in the tenancy no. longer remains and it seized to exist. 

 16. Considering the facts, circumstances and evidence as discussed above I find that Shafizuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs had been in exclusive possession of the suit land measuring .44 decimals of land of R.S . and S.A. Plot No. 469 corresponding to C.S. Plot No. 666 and BRS Plot No. 1088 by purchase since 1923 and after him the plaintiffs have been in exclusive possession thereof and thereby the plaintiffs acquired their valid title to the suit land. Since co-sharership in the tenancy seized to exist and in spite of having their exclusive title and possession in the suit land since the names of the defendants have been recorded in the hal BRS khatian No. 282 (Ext. 6) along with the names of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit land the title of the plaintiffs thereto is found to have been clouded and when the defendants on the basis of that wrong BRS Khatian No. 282 (Ext. 6) threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession of the suit land , the plaintiffs are en-titled to seek relief in a suit for declaratory relief with a view to removing the cloud on their title created due to wrong recording of ROR, because in such a suit declaration of title is all that the plaintiffs require, the plaintiffs may also seek for injunction along with the declaration of title if there is threat of dispossession. So the plaintiffs are not called upon to ask for consequential relief by way of partition.

For the Appellants: Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record.

full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J. :-This appeal by leave granted on 8.11.1995 is for consideration of the submissions of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant namely, first, that the area of the C.S. Khatian No. 191 was 5.74 which has been recorded in the two R.S. Khatian No. 690 with an area of 4.50 acres and R.S. Khatian No. 691 with an area of 1.24 acres and the contesting defendant Respondent No. 1 claimed only 1.24 acres of R.S. Khatian No. 691 which is the part and parcel of the C.S. Khatian No. 191 and this was never denied by the defendant-respondent either in the lower court or in the lower appellate court and, as such, the question of identity and repayment does not arise at the revisional stage, secondly, that the lower appellate Court after considering the evidence both oral and documentary found possession of the plaintiff in the suit land but the High Court Division on misappreciation of the evidence on record most illegally held that the lower appellate court's finding of possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land was contrary to material evidence on record and this finding of the High Court Division is wit:,--L airy iiasi3 whatsoever and lastly, that both the trial court and the lower appellate court, found possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and this finding of fact ought not to have been altered by the High Court Division in the revisional jurisdiction. 

 2. Plaintiff-appellants filed a suit for declaration of title stating, inter alia, that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 191 measuring 5.74 decimals was acquired by Tajumuddin Matbar on the basis of registered Patta dated 7th Aswin, 1281 B.S.: that Tajumuddin Matbar died before C.S. operation leaving one son Panjat All and one daughter Pearjan and after the death of his father Panjat Ali being a minor lived with his sister Pearjan who was married in the house of Nizamuddin. father-in-law of Pearjan and accordingly Nizamuddin became the de-facto guardian of Panjat Ali and, thus the property acquired by Tajumuddin Matbar on the basis of Patta dated 7th Aswin, 1281 B.S. was under the management and control of Nizamuddin and during the time of C.S. record aforesaid Patta land in C.S. Khatian No.191 was recorded in the names, Nizamuddin 1/3rd share. Ahmed (brother of Nizamuddin) 1/3rd share and Panjat Ali 1/3rd share although the property ought to have been recorded in 2/3rd share in the name of Panjat Ali and in 1/3rd share in the name of Pearjan; that immediately after the C.S. record Panjat Ali died leaving his sister Pearjan as his sole heir and accordingly Pearjan became the sole owner of the entire property left by Tajumuddin Matbar and thereafter Pearjan died leaving behind one son Hakimuddin who also was killed and survived by his two sons namely, Nurul Huq and Shamsul Huq, present plaintiff-appellants, and one daughter Noor Meher and a widow Rupjan and during the life time of Noor Meher and Rupjan they gifted their share to the plaintiff and thus the plain-tiffs became the sole owners of the property recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 191; that it has been further stated in the plaint that during R.S. operation the plaintiffs were minor and the land of C.S. Khatian No. 191 was also wrongly recorded in R.S. Khatian Nos. 690 and 691 which was subsequently recorded in S.A. Khatian Nos. 836 and 311 and though the entire land ought to have been recorded in the names of the plaintiffs but only 2 annas 15 gondas share of R.S. Khatian No. 690 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 830 has been recorded in the name of the plaintiff and the other recorded persons have or had no title and possession in any portion of the lands in R.S. as well as in S.A. Khatian of the suit land. 

 3. Defendant No. 6, Lutfor Rahman contested the suit claiming only 1.24 acres of S.A. Khatian No. 311 on the allegation that the R.S. recorded tenant Rahimjan made kolraiyati pattan of 1.24 acres of land to Kaisar Ahmed who is the recorded tenant of S.A. Khatian No. 311 and subsequently Kaisar Ahmed sold the land to Defendant No. 6. None of the defendants except Defendant No. 6 denied the title and possession of the plaintiffs. The further contention of Defendant No. 6 is that Tajumuddin had 1/3rd share in the suit property who died leaving a son Panjat Ali and daughter Pearjan; that Panjat Ali died leaving a sister Pearjan as his sole heir, Nizamuddin and Ahmed All had 2/3rd shares in the Khatian as per C.S. Khatian; that Nizamuddin died leaving two sons Aptar Ali and Amzad Ali and Amzad All died leaving behind three sons, three daughters and a wife, Ahmed Ali Heba gifted the entire share to Panjat Ali; that Pearjan and the heirs of Amjad Ali settled 1.23 acres of land with one Rahimjan in 1316 B.S. at a jama of Tk. 16/- and Rahimjan had been in possession of the suit land since her pattan. Rahimjan again settled 1.40 acres of land to Kaisar Ahmed by registered patta dated 10th Baisakh, 1352 B.S. and 1.24 acres of land stood recorded in the name of Kaisar Ahmed correctly that while in possession in that land Kaisar Ahmed sold his land to Defendant No. 6 by a kabala dated 27th Aswin, 1374 B.S. and Defendant No. 6 have been possessing the same since then. The plaintiffs filed a Partition suit being T.S. No. 184 of 1960 which was dis-missed; that thereafter another T.S. No. 207 of 1979 was filed which was also dis-missed. The present suit has also been brought on some false allegations and the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Mr. M. Shamsul Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant has taken us though the judgments of the Courts below, the plaint and the relevant papers on record and submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in making out a third case that the suit land can-not be definitely ascertained without relayment with the land of patta dated 17th Aswin, 1281 B.S. in order to see as to whether the land was identical or not inasmuch as in view of the rent receipt Ext. E series lead to a presumption of possession in favour of the defendant the findings of the lower appellate Court regarding possession of the plaintiff was contrary to the evidence on record. The learned Advocate further submits that the finding as to the possession of the final Court of fact has been disturbed by the High Court Division on misappreciation of the evidence on record inasmuch as the D. Ws. have themselves supported the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land and as such the finding of the High Court Division is not only contrary to the material evidence on record but without any basis whatsoever. 

 6. Mr. Menhazuddin Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents has however relying on Ext. B the certified copy of patta dated 10th Baisak 1352 B.S. and Ext. C kabala dated 27th Aswin 1374 B.S. has sought to argue that Rahimjan, the predecessor of Kaisar Ahmed has obtained the settlement of 1.23 acres of land on 23.4.1945 at a jama of Tk. 16/- and having possessed settled 1.40 acres in favour of Kaiser which has been correctly recorded in S.A. Khatian No. 311, who while in possession sold the same to Defendant No. 6 by kabala dated 27th Aswin 1374 B.S. Ext. C, who has been possessing mutating the name in the Khatian and payment of rent vide Ext. E series there was no illegality in the impugned judgment dismissing the suit setting aside the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below. 

 7. The plaintiffs based their claim on the basis of patta Ext. 1 dated 7th Aswin 1281 B.S. in favour of Tajumuddin Matbar who died before cadertral survey leaving son Panjat Ali and daughter Pearjan. Panjat All was minor and was under de-facto guardianship of Nizamuddin, father-in-law of Pearjan, sister of Panjat Ali who used to look after and manage the proper-ty left by Tajumuddin Matbar and fraudulently got it recorded 1/3rd share in his name and 1/3rd share in the name of his brother Ahmed All and 1/3rd share in the name of Panjat Ali instead of entire patta land of 5.74 decimals in the name of Panjat All and Pearjan in 2/3rd and 1/3rd share respectively and Panjat All died after C.S. operation leaving his sister Pearjan in his sole heir. Pearjan who died leaving behind one son Hakimuddin who while in possession was murdered in 1946 during the R.S. operation leaving behind minor Nurul Huq Plaintiff No. 1 and Shamsul Huq Plaintiff No. 2 and daughter Noor Meher and widow Rupjan. Noor Meher and Rupjan gifted their share in favour of the plaintiffs whereby plaintiffs became the owners of the entire land of C.S. Khatian No. 191. As such the R.S. Khatian Nos. 690 and 691 were also wrongly recorded the share of the plaintiffs pursuant to wrong C.S. Khatian and subsequently S.A. Khatian Nos. 836 and 311 were also recorded following wrong R.S. Khatian in spite of the recorders other than the plaintiffs having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land. The defendant, however, concocted certain documents such as alleged Solenama Ext. A. Patta Ext. B and sale deed Ext. C on the basis of alleged certificate case in respect of S.A. Khatian No. 836. 

 8. The Defendant No. 6 claiming 1.24 decimals of S.A. Khatian No. 311 asserted that R.S. recorded tenant Rahimjan made a kol raiyati patta to Kaiser Ahmed, the recorded tenant of S.A. Khatian No. 311 who sold the same in favour of Defendant No. 6-respondent. 

 9. The defendant alleged riyati patta by heirs of Amjad Ali, the successor-in-interest of Nazimuddin alleging pattan of 1.24 decimals dated 23.4.1945 corresponding to 1360 B.S. at a jama of Tk. 16/- in favour of Rahimjan, who while in possession settled 1.40 acres to Kaiser Ahmed by patta of dated 10th Baishak 1352 B.S. in whose name S.A. Khatian No. 311 was recorded who in his turn while in possession sold 1.24 decimal by kabala dated 27th Aswin 1374 B.S. Ext. C in favour of Defendant No. 6 who has been possessing. 

 13. The suit was for declaration of title of the plaintiff on assertion of possession and that C.S., R.S. and S.A. Khatians are wrong. Defendant has not disputed the quantum of land in patta Ext. 1 or the suit land as claimed by the plaintiff on the basis of the patta or that land of S.A. Khatian No. 311 did not form part of the land of patta Ext. 1 and as such there was no dispute that the suit land was not identical to the land patta Ext. 1 and accordingly no question of relayment in order to ascertain identity of the land was necessary. Thus the High Court Division erred in law in holding that in order to ascertain the suit land claimed by the plaintiff relayment is required and as that was not done by the plaintiff they failed to prove their claim as per pleading. 

 14. The plaintiff as well filed Exts. 2 and 3 as to payment of rent on the basis of patta dated 7th Aswin 1381 B.S. and the defendant No. 6 as well filed rent receipt Ext. E series to support their payment of rent in respect of the suit land of S.A. Khatian No. 311. In the case of Lal Meah being dead his heirs Momena Khaton and ors. Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Meah and ors. 28 DLR (AD) 61 it has been held that record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title of land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title. By itself, it is not an evidence of title. The presumption of correctness as available to the C.S. record of right in the name of Nazimuddin's  1/3rd share on the strength of Section 1038(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act has been rebutted as the defendants could not show any basis of record in view of patta Ext. 1 in favour of Tajumuddin, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs. Consequently there are also no basis of recording in R.S. and S.A. in the arnes of the recordees other than the plaintiffs. The defendant No. 6 also could not pro-duce any patta or rent receipt in support of the lease in favour of Rahimjan and as such the rent receipts Ext. D series could not confer any title on the defendant No. 6. The plaintiff led evidence of possession and the same has also been supported by D.Ws. Thus the presumption attached to C.S. has been rebutted and as such sub-sequent recording in R.S. and S.A. are of no legal consequence. The khatian being at best evidence of present possession could not be a document of title so as to confer right, title, and interest of the suit land. The defendant having failed to prove any basis of their title by any cogent material, the rent receipt Ext. E series are of no avail to them. When evidence was led in rebuttal of the presumption of correctness of entry in the record of right and the appellate Court below comes to a finding rebutting the presumption, the said finding being finding of fact, arrived at by the final Court of fact on consideration of the evidence on record, is not liable to be interfered with in revision as there was no error of law resulting in the error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The Court of appeal below has considered that no question of any partition in the suit is necessary, as the plaintiff has claimed the entire suit land and mores°, the suit was for declaration of title. 

 17. In view of the above, we hold that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land on the basis of their patta dated 17 Aswin 1281 B.S. but the C.S., R.S. and S.A. Khatian have wrongly recorded other recordees therein other than the plaintiffs.

lawyer:
Moksudur Rahman, Senior Advocate instructed by Md. Afiab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Appellants 
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record ----- For respondents No. 1-4 
Ex-parte -----Respondent Nos. 5-18
parties:
Mozirullah and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
Shafukuddin Ahmed and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff respondent filed the suit for declaration of title to. 1¼ acres of land (Schedule-ka) out of a total of .7 acres of land in khatian No. 5, plot No. 202 of Mouza 171 Dagan Bhuiyan (Schedule-kha) and for recovery of possession thereof. It is the case of the plaintiff that Hamid Ali and Azhar Ali, two brothers, by an amicable family partition arranged that Hamid Ali will get .7 acres of land in plot No. 202, khatian No. 5 (Schedule-kha) and other lands and that Azhar Ali will get .7 acres of land in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 both of Mouza Dagan Bhuiyan. Accordingly Azhar Ali while in exclusive ownership and possession of his allotted share sold his entire share in khatian No. 3 to Sirajul Haque and divested himself of all interests therein. Hamid Ali sold the entire .7 acres of land in plot No. 202 to his son Bashirullah by a registered deed dated 23-3-53. Bashirullah in his turn sold. 3½ acres out of .7 acres of land to his brother Hafizullah by a registered deed dated 26-10-60. Thereafter both bashirullah and Hafizullah sold the entire .7 acres of land to the plaintiff and his mother Hashmater Nessa by a registered deed dated 15-2-65. After the death of the plaintiff's mother the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the Schedule Kha land as her only heir. The Schedule kha land was originally anal land which the plaintiff converted into a bhiti land. He has constructed a kitchen in the bhiti and has stored some bricks and other house building materials. One Azizul Haque is occupying a portion thereof as a tenant under the plaintiff, the remaining land being in the khas possession of the plaintiff. On 16-12-78 defendant No. 1, a son of Azhar Ali, in the absence of the plaintiff, dispossessed him from the kutcha room in the north eastern portion of Schedule kha land measuring 1¼ acres which is the suit land the M. R. O. R. khatian has been prepared in the name of the plaintiff's vendor Bashirullah. The plaintiff has mutated his name and has been paying rent. The defendants have no right, title and interest in .7 acres of land of khatian No. 5. Hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 alone and defendant Nos. 2 and 5-7 together filed separate written statements and denied the plaintiff's case. They admitted that there was an amicable partition between the two brothers Hamid Ali and Azhar Ali and that Azhar Ali got in his share .7 acres of land in plot No. 197 in khatian No. 3, but it is their common case that Hamid Ali was given .7 acres of land in plot No. 192 of khatian No. 46 of the same Mouza and Hamid Ali subsequently transferred his entire share of .7 acres in khatian No. 46 to one Abdul Gani who made a structure on that land and let out to the Sub-Registrar's office of Dagan Bhuiyan. Defendant No. 1 stated in his written statement that his father Azahar Ali had. 3½ acres of share in plot No. 202 which he transferred to defendant No. 1 and his 5 brothers by two deeds of Hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 14-11-60 and 17-11-60. The six brothers raised the land, constructed a kutcha house and have been conducting therein the business of selling pan and firewood's since long. The plaintiff has not constructed any kutcha house on the north eastern corner of the plot. He has not stored any bricks there. No person called Azizul Huq has any construction there. There has been a fraudulent and wrong recording of rights in the recent khatinas. It is stated by defendant Nos. 2 and 5-7 in their written statement that .7 acres of land of plot No. 202 of khatian No. 5 (schedule kha) remained in the ejmali of Hamid Ali and Azhar Ali. Hamid Ali has no saleable interest in the land of khatian No. 5, plot No. 202 beyond his 8 annas interest i.e. 3½ acres. The plaintiff or his vendors Bashirullah and Hafizullah were never owners and possessors of more than 3½ acres of land in plot No. 202. The plaintiff is not entitled to any decree in the present suit. His remedy lies in a suit for partition seeking separate saham of his own portion of plot No. 202. The present suit is a test case to dislodge the defendants right, title and interest by way of making a foray into 1¼ acres out of .7 acres of land of plot No. 202. 

 The trial Court found title in favour of the plaintiff on consideration of Hamid Ali's document of sale to his son Bashirullah (Ext. 2(a) Bashirullahs's transfer of 3½ acres of land to his brother Hafizullah (Ext.2) and Bashirullah and Hafizullah's transfer of .7 acres of land to the plaintiff and his mother Ext. 2(B). The trial Court also found that the S.A. khatian (Ext.B) stands in the name of the plaintiff's vendor Bashirullah. It also found that the plaintiff mutated his name and paid rent to the Government by rent receipts (Ext. 3 series). Series of kabalas Ext. 5A to 5E show that Azhar Ali and his heirs sold away all the .7 acres of land which Azhar Ali obtained by way of partition in plot No. 197 of khatian No. 3. The trial Court also considered the case of the plaintiff's possession and subsequent dispossession and found that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case. 

 5. The appellant Court below found that there was no dispute between the parties that Azhar Ali got in his share .7 acres in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3. The dispute is whether Hamid Ali got .7 acres in plot No. 202, khatian No. 5, as claimed by the plaintiff or .7 acres of land in plot No. 192 No. 46, as claimed by the defendants Khatian No. 46 was exhibited by the plaintiff. The appellate Court below found that the plaintiff could not give any personal knowledge of the amicable partition and P.W. 3 Hafizullah and P.W. 8 Bashirullah also could not give proper relevant answers relating to partition in their cross-examination. The appellate Court below found that in khatian No. 46 there are 2.58 acres of land and Azhar Ali is the owner by purchase in respect of .83 acres of land therein. In this khatian Hamid Ali had no ownership. The appellant Court below noted the case of the defendants that Hamid Ali obtained .7 acres of land from khatian No. 46, plot No. 192. P.W. 8 Bashirullah, son of Hamid Ali admitted in his cross-examination that his father Hamid Ali used to possess .7 acres of land of khatian No. 46, plot No. 192 and that the said land is now being possessed by Abdul Gani. That is precisely the case of the defendants and the appellate Court below found that this admission by P.W. 8 weakened the case of the plaintiff The appellate Court below then considered Ext. 5 series, which were earlier considered by the trial Court and found that by Ext. 5 series the sons of Azhar Ali sold the land of plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 and also other lands of khatian No. 46 to various persons. In view of the fact that the defendants admit Azhar Ali's share in plot No. 197, khatian No. 3 and in view of the fact that Azhar Ali had independent title to .83 acres of land in khatian No. 46 the appellate Court below, contrary to the finding of the trial Court, found that Ext. 5 series do not support the plaintiff's case at all. The appellant Court below also held that since there was no partition by metes and bounds the recording of the land of khatian No. 5 in the name of Bashirullah and the mutation of it in favour of the plaintiff does not create any presumption. The defendants title thereto have not been injured thereby. 

 10. Mr. Khandkher Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the respondents has taken us through both the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate Court below. He could not show from the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate court below. He could not show from the judgment of the trial Court that the finding of title in favour of the plaintiff has been arrived at after considering the plaintiff's case on khatian No. 5 and the defendants case on khatian No. 46. Also he could not show that the trial Court at all adverted to the bone of contention between the parties, namely, whether Hamid Ali obtained in his share land from khatian No. 5 or from khatian No. 46. The trial Court seems to have decided the plaintiff's title in khatian No. 5 by finding that Azhar Ali and his heirs exhausted by sale his share in plot No. 197 which does not establish that Hamid Ali received in his share land of khatian No. 5. The trial Court has not considered the state of khatian No. 46 at al although it was exhibited by the plaintiff and has not dealt with the admission of P.W. 8 Bashirullah that his father used to possess .7 acres of land in khatian No. 46 and that the said land is now being possessed by Abdul Gani which is the defendants case. Mr. Ahmed also could not show that the lower appellate Court did not consider the oral and documentary evidence and that its conclusion about the plaintiff's title was arrived at abruptly. Nor he could show that the appellate Court below failed to consider the evidence as to possession and dispossession.
